Matthew 22:9.text: Go therefore to the crossroads and invite to the banquet as many as you can find.’

Matthew 22:10.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 22:10.text: So the servants went out into the streets and gathered everyone they could find, both evil and good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests.

Matthew 22:11.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 22:11.text: But when the king came in to see the guests, he spotted a man who was not dressed in wedding clothes.

Matthew 22:12.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 22:12.text: ‘Friend,’ he asked, ‘how did you get in here without wedding clothes?’ But the man was speechless.

Matthew 22:13.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 22:13.text: Then the king told the servants, ‘Tie him hand and foot, and throw him into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’

Matthew 22:14.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 22:14.text: For many are called, but few are chosen.”

Matthew 22:18.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 22:18.text: But Jesus knew their evil intent and said, “You hypocrites, why are you testing Me?

Matthew 22:19.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 22:19.text: Show Me the coin used for the tax.” And they brought Him a denarius.

Matthew 22:20.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 22:20.text: “Whose image is this,” He asked, “and whose inscription?”

Matthew 22:21.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 22:21.text: “Caesar’s,” they answered. So Jesus told them, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.”

Matthew 22:29.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 22:29.text: Jesus answered, “You are mistaken because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God.

Matthew 22:30.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 22:30.text: In the resurrection, people will neither marry nor be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like the angels in heaven.

Matthew 22:31.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 22:31.text: But concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what God said to you:

Matthew 22:32.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 22:32.text: ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? He is not the God of the dead, but of the living.”

Matthew 22:36.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 22:36.text: “Teacher, which commandment is the greatest in the Law?”

Matthew 22:37.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 22:37.text: Jesus declared, “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.’

Matthew 22:38.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 22:38.text: This is the first and greatest commandment.

Matthew 22:39.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 22:39.text: And the second is like it: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’

Matthew 22:40.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 22:40.text: All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments.”

Matthew 22:43.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 22:43.text: Jesus said to them, “How then does David in the Spirit call Him ‘Lord’? For he says:

Matthew 22:44.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 22:44.text: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.”’

Matthew 23:2.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:2.text: “The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat.

Matthew 23:3.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:3.text: So practice and observe everything they tell you. But do not do what they do, for they do not practice what they preach.

Matthew 23:4.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:4.text: They tie up heavy, burdensome loads and lay them on men’s shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to lift a finger to move them.

Matthew 23:5.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:5.text: All their deeds are done for men to see. They broaden their phylacteries and lengthen their tassels.

Matthew 23:6.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:6.text: They love the places of honor at banquets, the chief seats in the synagogues,

Matthew 23:7.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:7.text: the greetings in the marketplaces, and the title of ‘Rabbi’ by which they are addressed.

Matthew 23:8.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:8.text: But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi,’ for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers.

Matthew 23:9.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:9.text: And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.

Matthew 23:10.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:10.text: Nor are you to be called instructors, for you have one Instructor, the Christ.

Matthew 23:11.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:11.text: The greatest among you shall be your servant.

Matthew 23:12.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:12.text: For whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

Matthew 23:13.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:13.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You shut the kingdom of heaven in men’s faces. You yourselves do not enter, nor will you let in those who wish to enter.

Matthew 23:15.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:15.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You traverse land and sea to win a single convert, and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of hell as you are.

Matthew 23:16.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:16.text: Woe to you, blind guides! You say, ‘If anyone swears by the temple, it means nothing; but if anyone swears by the gold of the temple, he is bound by his oath.’

Matthew 23:17.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:17.text: You blind fools! Which is greater: the gold, or the temple that makes it sacred?

Matthew 23:18.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:18.text: And you say, ‘If anyone swears by the altar, it means nothing; but if anyone swears by the gift on it, he is bound by his oath.’

Matthew 23:19.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:19.text: You blind men! Which is greater: the gift, or the altar that makes it sacred?

Matthew 23:20.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:20.text: So then, he who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it.

Matthew 23:21.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:21.text: And he who swears by the temple swears by it and by the One who dwells in it.

Matthew 23:22.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:22.text: And he who swears by heaven swears by God’s throne and by the One who sits on it.

Matthew 23:23.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:23.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You pay tithes of mint, dill, and cumin. But you have disregarded the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faithfulness. You should have practiced the latter, without neglecting the former.

Matthew 23:24.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:24.text: You blind guides! You strain out a gnat but swallow a camel.

Matthew 23:25.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:25.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence.

Matthew 23:26.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:26.text: Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and dish, so that the outside may become clean as well.

Matthew 23:27.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:27.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You are like whitewashed tombs, which look beautiful on the outside but on the inside are full of dead men’s bones and every kind of impurity.

Matthew 23:28.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:28.text: In the same way, on the outside you appear to be righteous, but on the inside you are full of hypocrisy and wickedness.

Matthew 23:29.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:29.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You build tombs for the prophets and decorate the monuments of the righteous.

Matthew 23:30.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:30.text: And you say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partners with them in shedding the blood of the prophets.’

Matthew 23:31.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:31.text: So you testify against yourselves that you are the sons of those who murdered the prophets.

Matthew 23:32.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:32.text: Fill up, then, the measure of the sin of your fathers.

Matthew 23:33.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:33.text: You snakes! You brood of vipers! How will you escape the sentence of hell?

Matthew 23:34.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:34.text: Because of this, I am sending you prophets and wise men and teachers. Some of them you will kill and crucify, and others you will flog in your synagogues and persecute from town to town.

Matthew 23:35.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:35.text: And so upon you will come all the righteous blood shed on earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah, whom you murdered between the temple and the altar.

Matthew 23:36.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:36.text: Truly I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation.

Matthew 23:37.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:37.text: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I have longed to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!

Matthew 23:38.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:38.text: Look, your house is left to you desolate.

Matthew 23:39.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 23:39.text: For I tell you that you will not see Me again until you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.’”

Matthew 24:2.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:2.text: “Do you see all these things?” He replied. “Truly I tell you, not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.”

Matthew 24:3.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:3.text: While Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately. “Tell us,” they said, “when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of Your coming and of the end of the age?”

Matthew 24:4.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:4.text: Jesus answered, “See to it that no one deceives you.

Matthew 24:5.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:5.text: For many will come in My name, claiming, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will deceive many.

Matthew 24:6.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:6.text: You will hear of wars and rumors of wars, but see to it that you are not alarmed. These things must happen, but the end is still to come.

Matthew 24:7.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:7.text: Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be famines and earthquakes in various places.

Matthew 24:8.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:8.text: All these are the beginning of birth pains.

Matthew 24:9.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:9.text: Then they will deliver you over to be persecuted and killed, and you will be hated by all nations because of My name.

Matthew 24:10.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:10.text: At that time many will fall away and will betray and hate one another,

Matthew 24:11.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:11.text: and many false prophets will arise and deceive many.

Matthew 24:12.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:12.text: Because of the multiplication of wickedness, the love of most will grow cold.

Matthew 24:13.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:13.text: But the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.

Matthew 24:14.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:14.text: And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.

Matthew 24:15.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:15.text: So when you see standing in the holy place ‘the abomination of desolation,’ spoken of by the prophet Daniel (let the reader understand),

Matthew 24:16.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:16.text: then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.

Matthew 24:17.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:17.text: Let no one on the housetop come down to retrieve anything from his house.

Matthew 24:18.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:18.text: And let no one in the field return for his cloak.

Matthew 24:19.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:19.text: How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers!

Matthew 24:20.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:20.text: Pray that your flight will not occur in the winter or on the Sabbath.

Matthew 24:21.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:21.text: For at that time there will be great tribulation, unseen from the beginning of the world until now, and never to be seen again.

Matthew 24:22.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:22.text: If those days had not been cut short, nobody would be saved. But for the sake of the elect, those days will be cut short.

Matthew 24:23.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:23.text: At that time, if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘There He is!’ do not believe it.

Matthew 24:24.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:24.text: For false Christs and false prophets will appear and perform great signs and wonders to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.

Matthew 24:25.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:25.text: See, I have told you in advance.

Matthew 24:26.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:26.text: So if they tell you, ‘There He is, in the wilderness,’ do not go out, or, ‘Here He is, in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it.

Matthew 24:27.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:27.text: For just as the lightning comes from the east and flashes as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.

Matthew 24:28.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:28.text: Wherever there is a carcass, there the vultures will gather.

Matthew 24:29.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:29.text: Immediately after the tribulation of those days: ‘The sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light; the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.’

Matthew 24:30.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:30.text: At that time the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and all the tribes of the earth will mourn. They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.

Matthew 24:31.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:31.text: And He will send out His angels with a loud trumpet call, and they will gather His elect from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.

Matthew 24:32.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:32.text: Now learn this lesson from the fig tree: As soon as its branches become tender and sprout leaves, you know that summer is near.

Matthew 24:33.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:33.text: So also, when you see all these things, you will know that He is near, right at the door.

Matthew 24:34.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:34.text: Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened.

Matthew 24:35.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:35.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away.

Matthew 24:36.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:36.text: No one knows about that day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.

Matthew 24:37.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:37.text: As it was in the days of Noah, so will it be at the coming of the Son of Man.

Matthew 24:38.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:38.text: For in the days before the flood, people were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark.

Matthew 24:39.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:39.text: And they were oblivious until the flood came and swept them all away. So will it be at the coming of the Son of Man.

Matthew 24:40.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:40.text: Two men will be in the field: one will be taken and the other left.

Matthew 24:41.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:41.text: Two women will be grinding at the mill: one will be taken and the other left.

Matthew 24:42.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:42.text: Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day on which your Lord will come.

Matthew 24:43.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:43.text: But understand this: If the homeowner had known in which watch of the night the thief was coming, he would have kept watch and would not have let his house be broken into.

Matthew 24:44.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:44.text: For this reason, you also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.

Matthew 24:45.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:45.text: Who then is the faithful and wise servant, whom the master has put in charge of his household, to give the others their food at the proper time?

Matthew 24:46.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:46.text: Blessed is that servant whose master finds him doing so when he returns.

Matthew 24:47.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:47.text: Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.

Matthew 24:48.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:48.text: But suppose that servant is wicked and says in his heart, ‘My master will be away a long time.’

Matthew 24:49.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:49.text: And he begins to beat his fellow servants and to eat and drink with drunkards.

Matthew 24:50.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:50.text: The master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not anticipate.

Matthew 24:51.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 24:51.text: Then he will cut him to pieces and assign him a place with the hypocrites, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

Matthew 25:1.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:1.text: “At that time the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.

Matthew 25:2.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:2.text: Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.

Matthew 25:3.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:3.text: The foolish ones took their lamps but did not take along any extra oil.

Matthew 25:4.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:4.text: But the wise ones took oil in flasks along with their lamps.

Matthew 25:5.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:5.text: When the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and fell asleep.

Matthew 25:6.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:6.text: At midnight the cry rang out: ‘Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!’

Matthew 25:7.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:7.text: Then all the virgins woke up and trimmed their lamps.

Matthew 25:8.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:8.text: The foolish ones said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil; our lamps are going out.’

Matthew 25:9.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:9.text: ‘No,’ said the wise ones, ‘or there may not be enough for both us and you. Instead, go to those who sell oil and buy some for yourselves.’

Matthew 25:10.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:10.text: But while they were on their way to buy it, the bridegroom arrived. Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding banquet, and the door was shut.

Matthew 25:11.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:11.text: Later the other virgins arrived and said, ‘Lord, lord, open the door for us!’

Matthew 25:12.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:12.text: But he replied, ‘Truly I tell you, I do not know you.’

Matthew 25:13.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:13.text: Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day or the hour.

Matthew 25:14.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:14.text: For it is just like a man going on a journey, who called his servants and entrusted them with his possessions.

Matthew 25:15.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:15.text: To one he gave five talents, to another two talents, and to another one talent—each according to his own ability. And he went on his journey.

Matthew 25:16.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:16.text: The servant who had received the five talents went at once and put them to work and gained five more.

Matthew 25:17.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:17.text: Likewise, the one with the two talents gained two more.

Matthew 25:18.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:18.text: But the servant who had received the one talent went off, dug a hole in the ground, and hid his master’s money.

Matthew 25:19.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:19.text: After a long time the master of those servants returned and settled accounts with them.

Matthew 25:20.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:20.text: The servant who had received the five talents came and presented five more. ‘Master,’ he said, ‘you entrusted me with five talents. See, I have gained five more.’

Matthew 25:21.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:21.text: His master replied, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your master!’

Matthew 25:22.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:22.text: The servant who had received the two talents also came and said, ‘Master, you entrusted me with two talents. See, I have gained two more.’

Matthew 25:23.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:23.text: His master replied, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your master!’

Matthew 25:24.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:24.text: Finally, the servant who had received the one talent came and said, ‘Master, I knew that you are a hard man, reaping where you have not sown and gathering where you have not scattered seed.

Matthew 25:25.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:25.text: So I was afraid and went out and hid your talent in the ground. See, you have what belongs to you.’

Matthew 25:26.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:26.text: ‘You wicked, lazy servant!’ replied his master. ‘You knew that I reap where I have not sown and gather where I have not scattered seed.

Matthew 25:27.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:27.text: Then you should have deposited my money with the bankers, and on my return I would have received it back with interest.

Matthew 25:28.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:28.text: Therefore take the talent from him and give it to the one who has ten talents.

Matthew 25:29.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:29.text: For everyone who has will be given more, and he will have an abundance. But the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.

Matthew 25:30.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:30.text: And throw that worthless servant into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’

Matthew 25:31.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:31.text: When the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him, He will sit on His glorious throne.

Matthew 25:32.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:32.text: All the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate the people one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.

Matthew 25:33.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:33.text: He will place the sheep on His right and the goats on His left.

Matthew 25:34.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:34.text: Then the King will say to those on His right, ‘Come, you who are blessed by My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.

Matthew 25:35.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:35.text: For I was hungry and you gave Me something to eat, I was thirsty and you gave Me something to drink, I was a stranger and you took Me in,

Matthew 25:36.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:36.text: I was naked and you clothed Me, I was sick and you looked after Me, I was in prison and you visited Me.’

Matthew 25:37.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:37.text: Then the righteous will answer Him, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You, or thirsty and give You something to drink?

Matthew 25:38.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:38.text: When did we see You a stranger and take You in, or naked and clothe You?

Matthew 25:39.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:39.text: When did we see You sick or in prison and visit You?’

Matthew 25:40.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:40.text: And the King will reply, ‘Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers of Mine, you did for Me.’

Matthew 25:41.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:41.text: Then He will say to those on His left, ‘Depart from Me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.

Matthew 25:42.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:42.text: For I was hungry and you gave Me nothing to eat, I was thirsty and you gave Me nothing to drink,

Matthew 25:43.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:43.text: I was a stranger and you did not take Me in, I was naked and you did not clothe Me, I was sick and in prison and you did not look after Me.’

Matthew 25:44.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:44.text: And they too will reply, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not minister to You?’

Matthew 25:45.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:45.text: Then the King will answer, ‘Truly I tell you, whatever you did not do for one of the least of these, you did not do for Me.’

Matthew 25:46.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 25:46.text: And they will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”

Matthew 26:2.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:2.text: “You know that the Passover is two days away, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.”

Matthew 26:10.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:10.text: Aware of this, Jesus asked, “Why are you bothering this woman? She has done a beautiful deed to Me.

Matthew 26:11.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:11.text: The poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have Me.

Matthew 26:12.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:12.text: By pouring this perfume on Me, she has prepared My body for burial.

Matthew 26:13.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:13.text: Truly I tell you, wherever this gospel is preached in all the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”

Matthew 26:17.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:17.text: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Where do You want us to prepare for You to eat the Passover?”

Matthew 26:18.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:18.text: He answered, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him that the Teacher says, ‘My time is near. I will keep the Passover with My disciples at your house.’”

Matthew 26:21.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:21.text: And while they were eating, He said to them, “Truly I tell you, one of you will betray Me.”

Matthew 26:22.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:22.text: They were deeply grieved and began to ask Him one after another, “Surely not I, Lord?”

Matthew 26:23.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:23.text: Jesus answered, “The one who has dipped his hand into the bowl with Me will betray Me.

Matthew 26:24.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:24.text: The Son of Man will go just as it is written about Him, but woe to that man by whom He is betrayed. It would be better for him if he had not been born.”

Matthew 26:25.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:25.text: Then Judas, who would betray Him, said, “Surely not I, Rabbi?” Jesus answered, “You have said it yourself.”

Matthew 26:26.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:26.text: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to the disciples, saying, “Take and eat; this is My body.”

Matthew 26:27.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:27.text: Then He took the cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, “Drink from it, all of you.

Matthew 26:28.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:28.text: This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.

Matthew 26:29.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:29.text: I tell you, I will not drink of this fruit of the vine from now on until that day when I drink it anew with you in My Father’s kingdom.”

Matthew 26:31.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:31.text: Then Jesus said to them, “This very night you will all fall away on account of Me. For it is written: ‘I will strike the Shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’

Matthew 26:32.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:32.text: But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”

Matthew 26:34.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:34.text: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus declared, “this very night, before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.”

Matthew 26:36.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:36.text: Then Jesus went with His disciples to a place called Gethsemane, and He told them, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”

Matthew 26:38.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:38.text: Then He said to them, “My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch with Me.”

Matthew 26:39.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:39.text: Going a little farther, He fell facedown and prayed, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me. Yet not as I will, but as You will.”

Matthew 26:40.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:40.text: Then Jesus returned to the disciples and found them sleeping. “Were you not able to keep watch with Me for one hour?” He asked Peter.

Matthew 26:41.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:41.text: “Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation. For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.”

Matthew 26:42.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:42.text: A second time He went away and prayed, “My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, may Your will be done.”

Matthew 26:48.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:48.text: Now the betrayer had arranged a signal with them: “The One I kiss is the man; arrest Him.”

Matthew 26:49.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:49.text: Going directly to Jesus, he said, “Greetings, Rabbi!” and kissed Him.

Matthew 26:50.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:50.text: “Friend,” Jesus replied, “do what you came for.” Then the men stepped forward, seized Jesus, and arrested Him.

Matthew 26:52.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:52.text: “Put your sword back in its place,” Jesus said to him. “For all who draw the sword will die by the sword.

Matthew 26:53.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:53.text: Are you not aware that I can call on My Father, and He will at once put at My disposal more than twelve legions of angels?

Matthew 26:54.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:54.text: But how then would the Scriptures be fulfilled that say it must happen this way?”

Matthew 26:55.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:55.text: At that time Jesus said to the crowd, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me as you would an outlaw? Every day I sat teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest Me.

Matthew 26:56.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:56.text: But this has all happened so that the writings of the prophets would be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples deserted Him and fled.

Matthew 26:63.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:63.text: But Jesus remained silent. Then the high priest said to Him, “I charge You under oath by the living God: Tell us if You are the Christ, the Son of God.”

Matthew 26:64.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:64.text: “You have said it yourself,” Jesus answered. “But I say to all of you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven.”

Matthew 26:75.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 26:75.text: Then Peter remembered the word that Jesus had spoken: “Before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.” And he went outside and wept bitterly.

Matthew 27:4.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 27:4.text: “I have sinned by betraying innocent blood,” he said. “What is that to us?” they replied. “You bear the responsibility.”

Matthew 27:11.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 27:11.text: Meanwhile Jesus stood before the governor, who questioned Him: “Are You the King of the Jews?” “You have said so,” Jesus replied.

Matthew 27:19.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 27:19.text: While Pilate was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent him this message: “Have nothing to do with that innocent man, for I have suffered terribly in a dream today because of Him.”

Matthew 27:29.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 27:29.text: And they twisted together a crown of thorns and set it on His head. They put a staff in His right hand, knelt down before Him, and mocked Him, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!”

Matthew 27:40.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 27:40.text: and saying, “You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, save Yourself! If You are the Son of God, come down from the cross!”

Matthew 27:42.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 27:42.text: “He saved others, but He cannot save Himself. He is the King of Israel! Let Him come down now from the cross, and we will believe in Him.

Matthew 27:43.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 27:43.text: He trusts in God. Let God deliver Him now if He wants Him. For He said, ‘I am the Son of God.’”

Matthew 27:46.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 27:46.text: About the ninth hour Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?” which means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”

Matthew 28:9.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 28:9.text: Suddenly Jesus met them and said, “Greetings!” They came to Him, grasped His feet, and worshiped Him.

Matthew 28:10.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 28:10.text: “Do not be afraid,” said Jesus. “Go and tell My brothers to go to Galilee. There they will see Me.”

Matthew 28:18.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 28:18.text: Then Jesus came to them and said, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me.

Matthew 28:19.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 28:19.text: Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,

Matthew 28:20.speaker: Jesus
Matthew 28:20.text: and teaching them to obey all that I have commanded you. And surely I am with you always, even to the end of the age.”

Mark 1:2.speaker: Jesus
Mark 1:2.text: As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: “Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way.”

Mark 1:3.speaker: Jesus
Mark 1:3.text: “A voice of one calling in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him.’”

Mark 1:7.speaker: Jesus
Mark 1:7.text: And he proclaimed: “After me will come One more powerful than I, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and untie.

Mark 1:8.speaker: Jesus
Mark 1:8.text: I baptize you with water, but He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”

Mark 1:11.speaker: Jesus
Mark 1:11.text: And a voice came from heaven: “You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased.”

Mark 1:15.speaker: Jesus
Mark 1:15.text: “The time is fulfilled,” He said, “and the kingdom of God is near. Repent and believe in the gospel!”

Mark 1:17.speaker: Jesus
Mark 1:17.text: “Come, follow Me,” Jesus said, “and I will make you fishers of men.”

Mark 1:25.speaker: Jesus
Mark 1:25.text: But Jesus rebuked the spirit. “Be silent!” He said. “Come out of him!”

Mark 1:27.speaker: Jesus
Mark 1:27.text: All the people were amazed and began to ask one another, “What is this? A new teaching with authority! He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him!”

Mark 1:38.speaker: Jesus
Mark 1:38.text: But Jesus answered, “Let us go on to the neighboring towns so I can preach there as well, for that is why I have come.”

Mark 1:40.speaker: Jesus
Mark 1:40.text: Then a leper came to Jesus, begging on his knees: “If You are willing, You can make me clean.”

Mark 1:41.speaker: Jesus
Mark 1:41.text: Moved with compassion, Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man. “I am willing,” He said. “Be clean!”

Mark 1:44.speaker: Jesus
Mark 1:44.text: “See that you don’t tell anyone. But go, show yourself to the priest and present the offering Moses prescribed for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.”

Mark 2:5.speaker: Jesus
Mark 2:5.text: When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”

Mark 2:7.speaker: Jesus
Mark 2:7.text: “Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?”

Mark 2:8.speaker: Jesus
Mark 2:8.text: At once Jesus knew in His spirit that they were thinking this way within themselves. “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?” He asked.

Mark 2:9.speaker: Jesus
Mark 2:9.text: “Which is easier: to say to a paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, pick up your mat, and walk’?

Mark 2:10.speaker: Jesus
Mark 2:10.text: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins...” He said to the paralytic,

Mark 2:11.speaker: Jesus
Mark 2:11.text: “I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”

Mark 2:12.speaker: Jesus
Mark 2:12.text: And immediately the man got up, picked up his mat, and walked out in front of them all. As a result, they were all astounded and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!”

Mark 2:14.speaker: Jesus
Mark 2:14.text: As He was walking along, He saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth. “Follow Me,” He told him, and Levi got up and followed Him.

Mark 2:16.speaker: Jesus
Mark 2:16.text: When the scribes who were Pharisees saw Jesus eating with these people, they asked His disciples, “Why does He eat with tax collectors and sinners?”

Mark 2:17.speaker: Jesus
Mark 2:17.text: On hearing this, Jesus told them, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”

Mark 2:18.speaker: Jesus
Mark 2:18.text: Now John’s disciples and the Pharisees were often fasting. So people came to Jesus and asked, “Why don’t Your disciples fast like John’s disciples and those of the Pharisees?”

Mark 2:19.speaker: Jesus
Mark 2:19.text: Jesus replied, “How can the guests of the bridegroom fast while He is with them? As long as He is with them, they cannot fast.

Mark 2:20.speaker: Jesus
Mark 2:20.text: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.

Mark 2:21.speaker: Jesus
Mark 2:21.text: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment. If he does, the new piece will pull away from the old, and a worse tear will result.

Mark 2:22.speaker: Jesus
Mark 2:22.text: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the wine will burst the skins, and both the wine and the wineskins will be ruined. Instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins.”

Mark 2:25.speaker: Jesus
Mark 2:25.text: Jesus replied, “Have you never read what David did when he and his companions were hungry and in need?

Mark 2:26.speaker: Jesus
Mark 2:26.text: During the high priesthood of Abiathar, he entered the house of God and ate the consecrated bread, which was lawful only for the priests. And he gave some to his companions as well.”

Mark 2:27.speaker: Jesus
Mark 2:27.text: Then Jesus declared, “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.

Mark 2:28.speaker: Jesus
Mark 2:28.text: Therefore, the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.”

Mark 3:3.speaker: Jesus
Mark 3:3.text: Then Jesus said to the man with the withered hand, “Stand up among us.”

Mark 3:4.speaker: Jesus
Mark 3:4.text: And He asked them, “Which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?” But they were silent.

Mark 3:5.speaker: Jesus
Mark 3:5.text: Jesus looked around at them with anger and sorrow at their hardness of heart. Then He said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” So he stretched it out, and it was restored.

Mark 3:17.speaker: Jesus
Mark 3:17.text: James son of Zebedee and his brother John (whom He named Boanerges, meaning “Sons of Thunder”),

Mark 3:21.speaker: Jesus
Mark 3:21.text: When His family heard about this, they went out to take custody of Him, saying, “He is out of His mind.”

Mark 3:22.speaker: Jesus
Mark 3:22.text: And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, “He is possessed by Beelzebul,” and, “By the prince of the demons He drives out demons.”

Mark 3:23.speaker: Jesus
Mark 3:23.text: So Jesus called them together and began to speak to them in parables: “How can Satan drive out Satan?

Mark 3:24.speaker: Jesus
Mark 3:24.text: If a kingdom is divided against itself, it cannot stand.

Mark 3:25.speaker: Jesus
Mark 3:25.text: If a house is divided against itself, it cannot stand.

Mark 3:26.speaker: Jesus
Mark 3:26.text: And if Satan is divided and rises against himself, he cannot stand; his end has come.

Mark 3:27.speaker: Jesus
Mark 3:27.text: Indeed, no one can enter a strong man’s house to steal his possessions unless he first ties up the strong man. Then he can plunder his house.

Mark 3:28.speaker: Jesus
Mark 3:28.text: Truly I tell you, the sons of men will be forgiven all sins and blasphemies, as many as they utter.

Mark 3:29.speaker: Jesus
Mark 3:29.text: But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven; he is guilty of eternal sin.”

Mark 3:30.speaker: Jesus
Mark 3:30.text: Jesus made this statement because they were saying, “He has an unclean spirit.”

Mark 3:32.speaker: Jesus
Mark 3:32.text: and a crowd was sitting around Him. “Look,” He was told, “Your mother and brothers are outside, asking for You.”

Mark 3:33.speaker: Jesus
Mark 3:33.text: But Jesus replied, “Who are My mother and My brothers?”

Mark 3:34.speaker: Jesus
Mark 3:34.text: Looking at those seated in a circle around Him, He said, “Here are My mother and My brothers!

Mark 3:35.speaker: Jesus
Mark 3:35.text: For whoever does the will of God is My brother and sister and mother.”

Mark 4:3.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:3.text: “Listen! A farmer went out to sow his seed.

Mark 4:4.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:4.text: And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured it.

Mark 4:5.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:5.text: Some fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil. It sprang up quickly because the soil was shallow.

Mark 4:6.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:6.text: But when the sun rose, the seedlings were scorched, and they withered because they had no root.

Mark 4:7.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:7.text: Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up and choked the seedlings, and they yielded no crop.

Mark 4:8.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:8.text: Still other seed fell on good soil, where it sprouted, grew up, and produced a crop—one bearing thirtyfold, another sixtyfold, and another a hundredfold.”

Mark 4:9.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:9.text: Then Jesus said, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”

Mark 4:11.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:11.text: He replied, “The mystery of the kingdom of God has been given to you, but to those on the outside everything is expressed in parables,

Mark 4:12.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:12.text: so that, ‘they may be ever seeing but never perceiving, and ever hearing but never understanding; otherwise they might turn and be forgiven.’”

Mark 4:13.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:13.text: Then Jesus said to them, “Do you not understand this parable? Then how will you understand any of the parables?

Mark 4:15.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:15.text: Some are like the seeds along the path, where the word is sown. As soon as they hear it, Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.

Mark 4:16.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:16.text: Some are like the seeds sown on rocky ground. They hear the word and at once receive it with joy.

Mark 4:17.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:17.text: But they themselves have no root, and they remain for only a season. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they quickly fall away.

Mark 4:18.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:18.text: Others are like the seeds sown among the thorns. They hear the word,

Mark 4:19.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:19.text: but the worries of this life, the deceitfulness of wealth, and the desire for other things come in and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.

Mark 4:20.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:20.text: Still others are like the seeds sown on good soil. They hear the word, receive it, and produce a crop—thirtyfold, sixtyfold, or a hundredfold.”

Mark 4:21.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:21.text: Jesus also said to them, “Does anyone bring in a lamp to put it under a basket or under a bed? Doesn’t he set it on a stand?

Mark 4:22.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:22.text: For there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not be brought to light.

Mark 4:23.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:23.text: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.”

Mark 4:24.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:24.text: He went on to say, “Pay attention to what you hear. With the measure you use, it will be measured to you, and even more will be added to you.

Mark 4:25.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:25.text: For whoever has will be given more. But whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.”

Mark 4:26.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:26.text: Jesus also said, “The kingdom of God is like a man who scatters seed on the ground.

Mark 4:27.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:27.text: Night and day he sleeps and wakes, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he knows not how.

Mark 4:28.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:28.text: All by itself the earth produces a crop—first the stalk, then the head, then grain that ripens within.

Mark 4:29.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:29.text: And as soon as the grain is ripe, he swings the sickle, because the harvest has come.”

Mark 4:30.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:30.text: Then He asked, “To what can we compare the kingdom of God? With what parable shall we present it?

Mark 4:31.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:31.text: It is like a mustard seed, which is the smallest of all seeds sown upon the earth.

Mark 4:32.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:32.text: But after it is planted, it grows to be the largest of all garden plants and puts forth great branches, so that the birds of the air nest in its shade.”

Mark 4:35.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:35.text: When that evening came, He said to His disciples, “Let us cross to the other side.”

Mark 4:39.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:39.text: Then Jesus got up and rebuked the wind and the sea. “Silence!” He commanded. “Be still!” And the wind died down, and it was perfectly calm.

Mark 4:40.speaker: Jesus
Mark 4:40.text: “Why are you so afraid?” He asked. “Do you still have no faith?”

Mark 5:7.speaker: Jesus
Mark 5:7.text: And he shouted in a loud voice, “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You before God not to torture me!”

Mark 5:8.speaker: Jesus
Mark 5:8.text: For Jesus had already declared, “Come out of this man, you unclean spirit!”

Mark 5:9.speaker: Jesus
Mark 5:9.text: “What is your name?” Jesus asked. “My name is Legion,” he replied, “for we are many.”

Mark 5:12.speaker: Jesus
Mark 5:12.text: So the demons begged Jesus, “Send us to the pigs, so that we may enter them.”

Mark 5:19.speaker: Jesus
Mark 5:19.text: But Jesus would not allow him. “Go home to your own people,” He said, “and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and what mercy He has shown you.”

Mark 5:23.speaker: Jesus
Mark 5:23.text: and pleaded with Him urgently, “My little daughter is near death. Please come and place Your hands on her, so that she will be healed and live.”

Mark 5:28.speaker: Jesus
Mark 5:28.text: For she kept saying, “If only I touch His garments, I will be healed.”

Mark 5:30.speaker: Jesus
Mark 5:30.text: At once Jesus was aware that power had gone out from Him. Turning to the crowd, He asked, “Who touched My garments?”

Mark 5:34.speaker: Jesus
Mark 5:34.text: “Daughter,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you. Go in peace and be free of your affliction.”

Mark 5:36.speaker: Jesus
Mark 5:36.text: But Jesus overheard their conversation and said to Jairus, “Do not be afraid; just believe.”

Mark 5:39.speaker: Jesus
Mark 5:39.text: He went inside and asked, “Why all this commotion and weeping? The child is not dead, but asleep.”

Mark 5:41.speaker: Jesus
Mark 5:41.text: Taking her by the hand, Jesus said, “Talitha koum!” which means, “Little girl, I say to you, get up!”

Mark 6:2.speaker: Jesus
Mark 6:2.text: When the Sabbath came, He began to teach in the synagogue, and many who heard Him were astonished. “Where did this man get these ideas?” they asked. “What is this wisdom He has been given? And how can He perform such miracles?

Mark 6:3.speaker: Jesus
Mark 6:3.text: Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary and the brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? Aren’t His sisters here with us as well?” And they took offense at Him.

Mark 6:4.speaker: Jesus
Mark 6:4.text: Then Jesus said to them, “Only in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own household is a prophet without honor.”

Mark 6:10.speaker: Jesus
Mark 6:10.text: And He told them, “When you enter a house, stay there until you leave that area.

Mark 6:11.speaker: Jesus
Mark 6:11.text: If anyone will not welcome you or listen to you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that place, as a testimony against them.”

Mark 6:14.speaker: Jesus
Mark 6:14.text: Now King Herod heard about this, for Jesus’ name had become well known, and people were saying, “John the Baptist has risen from the dead! That is why miraculous powers are at work in him.”

Mark 6:15.speaker: Jesus
Mark 6:15.text: Others were saying, “He is Elijah,” and still others, “He is a prophet, like one of the prophets of old.”

Mark 6:16.speaker: Jesus
Mark 6:16.text: But when Herod heard this, he said, “John, whom I beheaded, has risen from the dead!”

Mark 6:18.speaker: Jesus
Mark 6:18.text: For John had been telling Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife!”

Mark 6:31.speaker: Jesus
Mark 6:31.text: And He said to them, “Come with Me privately to a solitary place, and let us rest for a while.” For many people were coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat.

Mark 6:35.speaker: Jesus
Mark 6:35.text: By now the hour was already late. So the disciples came to Jesus and said, “This is a desolate place, and the hour is already late.

Mark 6:36.speaker: Jesus
Mark 6:36.text: Dismiss the crowd so they can go to the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves something to eat.”

Mark 6:37.speaker: Jesus
Mark 6:37.text: But Jesus told them, “You give them something to eat.” They asked Him, “Should we go out and spend two hundred denarii to give all of them bread to eat?”

Mark 6:38.speaker: Jesus
Mark 6:38.text: “Go and see how many loaves you have,” He told them. And after checking, they said, “Five—and two fish.”

Mark 6:50.speaker: Jesus
Mark 6:50.text: for they all saw Him and were terrified. But Jesus spoke up at once: “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”

Mark 7:5.speaker: Jesus
Mark 7:5.text: So the Pharisees and scribes questioned Jesus: “Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders? Instead, they eat with defiled hands.”

Mark 7:6.speaker: Jesus
Mark 7:6.text: Jesus answered them, “Isaiah prophesied correctly about you hypocrites, as it is written: ‘These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me.

Mark 7:7.speaker: Jesus
Mark 7:7.text: They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men.’

Mark 7:8.speaker: Jesus
Mark 7:8.text: You have disregarded the commandment of God to keep the tradition of men.”

Mark 7:9.speaker: Jesus
Mark 7:9.text: He went on to say, “You neatly set aside the command of God to maintain your own tradition.

Mark 7:10.speaker: Jesus
Mark 7:10.text: For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother’ and ‘Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.’

Mark 7:11.speaker: Jesus
Mark 7:11.text: But you say that if a man says to his father or mother, ‘Whatever you would have received from me is Corban’ (that is, a gift devoted to God),

Mark 7:12.speaker: Jesus
Mark 7:12.text: he is no longer permitted to do anything for his father or mother.

Mark 7:13.speaker: Jesus
Mark 7:13.text: Thus you nullify the word of God by the tradition you have handed down. And you do so in many such matters.”

Mark 7:14.speaker: Jesus
Mark 7:14.text: Once again Jesus called the crowd to Him and said, “All of you, listen to Me and understand:

Mark 7:15.speaker: Jesus
Mark 7:15.text: Nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him; but the things that come out of a man, these are what defile him.”

Mark 7:18.speaker: Jesus
Mark 7:18.text: “Are you still so dull?” He asked. “Do you not understand? Nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him,

Mark 7:19.speaker: Jesus
Mark 7:19.text: because it does not enter his heart, but it goes into the stomach and then is eliminated.” (Thus all foods are clean.)

Mark 7:20.speaker: Jesus
Mark 7:20.text: He continued: “What comes out of a man, that is what defiles him.

Mark 7:21.speaker: Jesus
Mark 7:21.text: For from within the hearts of men come evil thoughts, sexual immorality, theft, murder, adultery,

Mark 7:22.speaker: Jesus
Mark 7:22.text: greed, wickedness, deceit, debauchery, envy, slander, arrogance, and foolishness.

Mark 7:23.speaker: Jesus
Mark 7:23.text: All these evils come from within, and these are what defile a man.”

Mark 7:27.speaker: Jesus
Mark 7:27.text: “First let the children have their fill,” He said. “For it is not right to take the children’s bread and toss it to the dogs.”

Mark 7:29.speaker: Jesus
Mark 7:29.text: Then Jesus told her, “Because of this answer, you may go. The demon has left your daughter.”

Mark 7:34.speaker: Jesus
Mark 7:34.text: And looking up to heaven, He sighed deeply and said to him, “Ephphatha!” (which means, “Be opened!”).

Mark 8:2.speaker: Jesus
Mark 8:2.text: “I have compassion for this crowd, because they have already been with Me three days and have nothing to eat.

Mark 8:3.speaker: Jesus
Mark 8:3.text: If I send them home hungry, they will faint along the way. For some of them have come a great distance.”

Mark 8:5.speaker: Jesus
Mark 8:5.text: “How many loaves do you have?” Jesus asked. “Seven,” they replied.

Mark 8:12.speaker: Jesus
Mark 8:12.text: Jesus sighed deeply in His spirit and said, “Why does this generation demand a sign? Truly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.”

Mark 8:15.speaker: Jesus
Mark 8:15.text: “Watch out!” He cautioned them. “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod.”

Mark 8:17.speaker: Jesus
Mark 8:17.text: Aware of their conversation, Jesus asked them, “Why are you debating about having no bread? Do you still not see or understand? Do you have such hard hearts?

Mark 8:18.speaker: Jesus
Mark 8:18.text: ‘Having eyes, do you not see? And having ears, do you not hear?’ And do you not remember?

Mark 8:19.speaker: Jesus
Mark 8:19.text: When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many basketfuls of broken pieces did you collect?” “Twelve,” they answered.

Mark 8:23.speaker: Jesus
Mark 8:23.text: So He took the blind man by the hand and led him out of the village. Then He spit on the man’s eyes and placed His hands on him. “Can you see anything?” He asked.

Mark 8:26.speaker: Jesus
Mark 8:26.text: Jesus sent him home and said, “Do not go back into the village.”

Mark 8:27.speaker: Jesus
Mark 8:27.text: Then Jesus and His disciples went on to the villages around Caesarea Philippi. On the way, He questioned His disciples: “Who do people say I am?”

Mark 8:29.speaker: Jesus
Mark 8:29.text: “But what about you?” Jesus asked. “Who do you say I am?” Peter answered, “You are the Christ.”

Mark 8:33.speaker: Jesus
Mark 8:33.text: But Jesus, turning and looking at His disciples, rebuked Peter and said, “Get behind Me, Satan! For you do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men.”

Mark 8:34.speaker: Jesus
Mark 8:34.text: Then Jesus called the crowd to Him along with His disciples, and He told them, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me.

Mark 8:35.speaker: Jesus
Mark 8:35.text: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake and for the gospel will save it.

Mark 8:36.speaker: Jesus
Mark 8:36.text: What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet forfeit his soul?

Mark 8:37.speaker: Jesus
Mark 8:37.text: Or what can a man give in exchange for his soul?

Mark 8:38.speaker: Jesus
Mark 8:38.text: If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when He comes in His Father’s glory with the holy angels.”

Mark 9:1.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:1.text: Then Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, there are some standing here who will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God arrive with power.”

Mark 9:5.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:5.text: Peter said to Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us put up three shelters—one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”

Mark 9:7.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:7.text: Then a cloud appeared and enveloped them, and a voice came from the cloud: “This is My beloved Son. Listen to Him!”

Mark 9:11.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:11.text: And they asked Jesus, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”

Mark 9:12.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:12.text: He replied, “Elijah does indeed come first, and he restores all things. Why then is it written that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected?

Mark 9:13.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:13.text: But I tell you that Elijah has indeed come, and they have done to him whatever they wished, just as it is written about him.”

Mark 9:16.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:16.text: “What are you disputing with them?” He asked.

Mark 9:19.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:19.text: “O unbelieving generation!” Jesus replied. “How long must I remain with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy to Me.”

Mark 9:21.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:21.text: Jesus asked the boy’s father, “How long has this been with him?” “From childhood,” he said.

Mark 9:22.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:22.text: “It often throws him into the fire or into the water, trying to kill him. But if You can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.”

Mark 9:23.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:23.text: “If You can?” echoed Jesus. “All things are possible to him who believes!”

Mark 9:25.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:25.text: When Jesus saw that a crowd had come running, He rebuked the unclean spirit. “You deaf and mute spirit,” He said, “I command you to come out and never enter him again.”

Mark 9:28.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:28.text: After Jesus had gone into the house, His disciples asked Him privately, “Why couldn’t we drive it out?”

Mark 9:29.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:29.text: Jesus answered, “This kind cannot come out, except by prayer.”

Mark 9:31.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:31.text: because He was teaching His disciples. He told them, “The Son of Man will be delivered into the hands of men. They will kill Him, and after three days He will rise.”

Mark 9:33.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:33.text: Then they came to Capernaum. While Jesus was in the house, He asked them, “What were you discussing on the way?”

Mark 9:35.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:35.text: Sitting down, Jesus called the Twelve and said, “If anyone wants to be first, he must be the last of all and the servant of all.”

Mark 9:37.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:37.text: “Whoever welcomes one of these little children in My name welcomes Me, and whoever welcomes Me welcomes not only Me, but the One who sent Me.”

Mark 9:39.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:39.text: “Do not stop him,” Jesus replied. “For no one who performs a miracle in My name can turn around and speak evil of Me.

Mark 9:40.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:40.text: For whoever is not against us is for us.

Mark 9:41.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:41.text: Indeed, if anyone gives you even a cup of water because you bear the name of Christ, truly I tell you, he will never lose his reward.

Mark 9:42.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:42.text: But if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea.

Mark 9:43.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:43.text: If your hand causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life crippled than to have two hands and go into hell, into the unquenchable fire.

Mark 9:45.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:45.text: If your foot causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to have two feet and be thrown into hell.

Mark 9:47.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:47.text: And if your eye causes you to sin, pluck it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into hell,

Mark 9:48.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:48.text: where ‘their worm never dies, and the fire is never quenched.’

Mark 9:49.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:49.text: For everyone will be salted with fire.

Mark 9:50.speaker: Jesus
Mark 9:50.text: Salt is good, but if the salt loses its saltiness, with what will you season it? Have salt among yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”

Mark 10:2.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:2.text: Some Pharisees came to test Him. “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?” they inquired.

Mark 10:3.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:3.text: “What did Moses command you?” He replied.

Mark 10:5.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:5.text: But Jesus told them, “Moses wrote this commandment for you because of your hardness of heart.

Mark 10:6.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:6.text: However, from the beginning of creation, ‘God made them male and female.’

Mark 10:7.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:7.text: ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife,

Mark 10:8.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:8.text: and the two will become one flesh.’ So they are no longer two, but one flesh.

Mark 10:9.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:9.text: Therefore what God has joined together, let man not separate.”

Mark 10:11.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:11.text: So He told them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery against her.

Mark 10:12.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:12.text: And if a woman divorces her husband and marries another man, she commits adultery.”

Mark 10:14.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:14.text: But when Jesus saw this, He was indignant and told them, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

Mark 10:15.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:15.text: Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.”

Mark 10:17.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:17.text: As Jesus started on His way, a man ran up and knelt before Him. “Good Teacher,” he asked, “what must I do to inherit eternal life?”

Mark 10:18.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:18.text: “Why do you call Me good?” Jesus replied. “No one is good except God alone.

Mark 10:19.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:19.text: You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness, do not cheat others, honor your father and mother.’”

Mark 10:20.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:20.text: “Teacher,” he replied, “all these I have kept from my youth.”

Mark 10:21.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:21.text: Jesus looked at him, loved him, and said to him, “There is one thing you lack: Go, sell everything you own and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”

Mark 10:23.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:23.text: Then Jesus looked around and said to His disciples, “How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!”

Mark 10:24.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:24.text: And the disciples were amazed at His words. But Jesus said to them again, “Children, how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God!

Mark 10:25.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:25.text: It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”

Mark 10:27.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:27.text: Jesus looked at them and said, “With man this is impossible, but not with God. For all things are possible with God.”

Mark 10:29.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:29.text: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “no one who has left home or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields for My sake and for the gospel

Mark 10:30.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:30.text: will fail to receive a hundredfold in the present age—houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, along with persecutions—and in the age to come, eternal life.

Mark 10:31.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:31.text: But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.”

Mark 10:33.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:33.text: “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes. They will condemn Him to death and will deliver Him over to the Gentiles,

Mark 10:34.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:34.text: who will mock Him and spit on Him and flog Him and kill Him. And after three days He will rise again.”

Mark 10:35.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:35.text: Then James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to Jesus and declared, “Teacher, we want You to do for us whatever we ask.”

Mark 10:36.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:36.text: “What do you want Me to do for you?” He inquired.

Mark 10:38.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:38.text: “You do not know what you are asking,” Jesus replied. “Can you drink the cup I will drink, or be baptized with the baptism I will undergo?”

Mark 10:39.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:39.text: “We can,” the brothers answered. “You will drink the cup that I drink,” Jesus said, “and you will be baptized with the baptism that I undergo.

Mark 10:40.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:40.text: But to sit at My right or left is not Mine to grant. These seats belong to those for whom they have been prepared.”

Mark 10:42.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:42.text: So Jesus called them together and said, “You know that those regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their superiors exercise authority over them.

Mark 10:43.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:43.text: But it shall not be this way among you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,

Mark 10:44.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:44.text: and whoever wants to be first must be the slave of all.

Mark 10:45.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:45.text: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.”

Mark 10:47.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:47.text: When he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”

Mark 10:48.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:48.text: Many people admonished him to be silent, but he cried out all the louder, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”

Mark 10:49.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:49.text: Jesus stopped and said, “Call him.” So they called the blind man. “Take courage!” they said. “Get up! He is calling for you.”

Mark 10:51.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:51.text: “What do you want Me to do for you?” Jesus asked. “Rabboni,” said the blind man, “let me see again.”

Mark 10:52.speaker: Jesus
Mark 10:52.text: “Go,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you.” And immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus along the road.

Mark 11:9.speaker: Jesus
Mark 11:9.text: The ones who went ahead and those who followed were shouting: “Hosanna!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!”

Mark 11:10.speaker: Jesus
Mark 11:10.text: “Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!” “Hosanna in the highest!”

Mark 11:14.speaker: Jesus
Mark 11:14.text: Then He said to the tree, “May no one ever eat of your fruit again.” And His disciples heard this statement.

Mark 11:17.speaker: Jesus
Mark 11:17.text: Then Jesus began to teach them, and He declared, “Is it not written: ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations’? But you have made it ‘a den of robbers.’”

Mark 11:22.speaker: Jesus
Mark 11:22.text: “Have faith in God,” Jesus said to them.

Mark 11:23.speaker: Jesus
Mark 11:23.text: “Truly I tell you that if anyone says to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ and has no doubt in his heart but believes that it will happen, it will be done for him.

Mark 11:24.speaker: Jesus
Mark 11:24.text: Therefore I tell you, whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.

Mark 11:25.speaker: Jesus
Mark 11:25.text: And when you stand to pray, if you hold anything against another, forgive it, so that your Father in heaven will forgive your trespasses as well.”

Mark 11:29.speaker: Jesus
Mark 11:29.text: “I will ask you one question,” Jesus replied, “and if you answer Me, I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.

Mark 11:30.speaker: Jesus
Mark 11:30.text: John’s baptism—was it from heaven or from men? Answer Me!”

Mark 11:31.speaker: Jesus
Mark 11:31.text: They deliberated among themselves what they should answer: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’

Mark 11:32.speaker: Jesus
Mark 11:32.text: But if we say, ‘From men’...” they were afraid of the people, for they all held that John truly was a prophet.

Mark 11:33.speaker: Jesus
Mark 11:33.text: So they answered, “We do not know.” And Jesus replied, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.”

Mark 12:1.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:1.text: Then Jesus began to speak to them in parables: “A man planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a wine vat, and built a watchtower. Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.

Mark 12:2.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:2.text: At harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard.

Mark 12:3.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:3.text: But they seized the servant, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.

Mark 12:4.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:4.text: Then he sent them another servant, and they struck him over the head and treated him shamefully.

Mark 12:5.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:5.text: He sent still another, and this one they killed. He sent many others; some they beat and others they killed.

Mark 12:6.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:6.text: Finally, having one beloved son, he sent him to them. ‘They will respect my son,’ he said.

Mark 12:7.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:7.text: But the tenants said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’

Mark 12:8.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:8.text: So they seized the son, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.

Mark 12:9.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:9.text: What then will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and kill those tenants and give the vineyard to others.

Mark 12:10.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:10.text: Have you never read this Scripture: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.

Mark 12:11.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:11.text: This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?”

Mark 12:15.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:15.text: But Jesus saw through their hypocrisy and said, “Why are you testing Me? Bring Me a denarius to inspect.”

Mark 12:16.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:16.text: So they brought it, and He asked them, “Whose image is this? And whose inscription?” “Caesar’s,” they answered.

Mark 12:17.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:17.text: Then Jesus told them, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.” And they marveled at Him.

Mark 12:19.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:19.text: “Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, the man is to marry his brother’s widow and raise up offspring for him.

Mark 12:20.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:20.text: Now there were seven brothers. The first one married and died, leaving no children.

Mark 12:21.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:21.text: Then the second one married the widow, but he also died and left no children. And the third did likewise.

Mark 12:22.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:22.text: In this way, none of the seven left any children. And last of all, the woman died.

Mark 12:23.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:23.text: In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be? For all seven were married to her.”

Mark 12:24.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:24.text: Jesus said to them, “Aren’t you mistaken, because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God?

Mark 12:25.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:25.text: When the dead rise, they will neither marry nor be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like the angels in heaven.

Mark 12:26.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:26.text: But concerning the dead rising, have you not read about the burning bush in the Book of Moses, how God told him, ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?

Mark 12:27.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:27.text: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are badly mistaken!”

Mark 12:28.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:28.text: Now one of the scribes had come up and heard their debate. Noticing how well Jesus had answered them, he asked Him, “Which commandment is the most important of all?”

Mark 12:29.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:29.text: Jesus replied, “This is the most important: ‘Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One.

Mark 12:30.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:30.text: Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength.’

Mark 12:31.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:31.text: The second is this: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’ No other commandment is greater than these.”

Mark 12:34.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:34.text: When Jesus saw that the man had answered wisely, He said, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” And no one dared to question Him any further.

Mark 12:35.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:35.text: While Jesus was teaching in the temple courts, He asked, “How can the scribes say that the Christ is the Son of David?

Mark 12:36.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:36.text: Speaking by the Holy Spirit, David himself declared: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.”’

Mark 12:38.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:38.text: In His teaching Jesus also said, “Watch out for the scribes. They like to walk around in long robes, to receive greetings in the marketplaces,

Mark 12:39.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:39.text: and to have the chief seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at banquets.

Mark 12:40.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:40.text: They defraud widows of their houses, and for a show make lengthy prayers. These men will receive greater condemnation.”

Mark 12:43.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:43.text: Jesus called His disciples to Him and said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put more than all the others into the treasury.

Mark 12:44.speaker: Jesus
Mark 12:44.text: For they all contributed out of their surplus, but she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on.”

Mark 13:2.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:2.text: “Do you see all these great buildings?” Jesus replied. “Not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.”

Mark 13:5.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:5.text: Jesus began by telling them, “See to it that no one deceives you.

Mark 13:6.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:6.text: Many will come in My name, claiming, ‘I am He,’ and will deceive many.

Mark 13:7.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:7.text: When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, do not be alarmed. These things must happen, but the end is still to come.

Mark 13:8.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:8.text: Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places, as well as famines. These are the beginning of birth pains.

Mark 13:9.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:9.text: So be on your guard. You will be delivered over to the councils and beaten in the synagogues. On My account you will stand before governors and kings as witnesses to them.

Mark 13:10.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:10.text: And the gospel must first be proclaimed to all the nations.

Mark 13:11.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:11.text: But when they arrest you and hand you over, do not worry beforehand what to say. Instead, speak whatever you are given at that time, for it will not be you speaking, but the Holy Spirit.

Mark 13:12.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:12.text: Brother will betray brother to death, and a father his child. Children will rise against their parents and have them put to death.

Mark 13:13.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:13.text: You will be hated by everyone because of My name, but the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.

Mark 13:14.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:14.text: So when you see the abomination of desolation standing where it should not be (let the reader understand), then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.

Mark 13:15.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:15.text: Let no one on the housetop go back inside to retrieve anything from his house.

Mark 13:16.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:16.text: And let no one in the field return for his cloak.

Mark 13:17.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:17.text: How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers!

Mark 13:18.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:18.text: Pray that this will not occur in the winter.

Mark 13:19.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:19.text: For those will be days of tribulation unseen from the beginning of God’s creation until now, and never to be seen again.

Mark 13:20.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:20.text: If the Lord had not cut short those days, nobody would be saved. But for the sake of the elect, whom He has chosen, He has cut them short.

Mark 13:21.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:21.text: At that time if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘There He is!’ do not believe it.

Mark 13:22.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:22.text: For false Christs and false prophets will appear and perform signs and wonders to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.

Mark 13:23.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:23.text: So be on your guard; I have told you everything in advance.

Mark 13:24.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:24.text: But in those days, after that tribulation: ‘The sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light;

Mark 13:25.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:25.text: the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.’

Mark 13:26.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:26.text: At that time they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds with great power and glory.

Mark 13:27.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:27.text: And He will send out the angels to gather His elect from the four winds, from the ends of the earth to the ends of heaven.

Mark 13:28.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:28.text: Now learn this lesson from the fig tree: As soon as its branches become tender and sprout leaves, you know that summer is near.

Mark 13:29.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:29.text: So also, when you see these things happening, know that He is near, right at the door.

Mark 13:30.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:30.text: Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened.

Mark 13:31.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:31.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away.

Mark 13:32.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:32.text: No one knows about that day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.

Mark 13:33.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:33.text: Be on your guard and stay alert! For you do not know when the appointed time will come.

Mark 13:34.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:34.text: It is like a man going on a journey who left his house, put each servant in charge of his own task, and instructed the doorkeeper to keep watch.

Mark 13:35.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:35.text: Therefore keep watch, because you do not know when the master of the house will return—whether in the evening, at midnight, when the rooster crows, or in the morning.

Mark 13:36.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:36.text: Otherwise, he may arrive without notice and find you sleeping.

Mark 13:37.speaker: Jesus
Mark 13:37.text: And what I say to you, I say to everyone: Keep watch!”

Mark 14:4.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:4.text: Some of those present, however, expressed their indignation to one another: “Why this waste of perfume?

Mark 14:5.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:5.text: It could have been sold for over three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor.” And they scolded her.

Mark 14:6.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:6.text: But Jesus said, “Leave her alone; why are you bothering her? She has done a beautiful deed to Me.

Mark 14:7.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:7.text: The poor you will always have with you, and you can help them whenever you want. But you will not always have Me.

Mark 14:8.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:8.text: She has done what she could to anoint My body in advance of My burial.

Mark 14:9.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:9.text: And truly I tell you, wherever the gospel is preached in all the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”

Mark 14:12.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:12.text: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed, Jesus’ disciples asked Him, “Where do You want us to prepare for You to eat the Passover?”

Mark 14:18.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:18.text: And while they were reclining and eating, Jesus said, “Truly I tell you, one of you who is eating with Me will betray Me.”

Mark 14:19.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:19.text: They began to be grieved and to ask Him one after another, “Surely not I?”

Mark 14:20.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:20.text: He answered, “It is one of the Twelve—the one who is dipping his hand into the bowl with Me.

Mark 14:21.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:21.text: The Son of Man will go just as it is written about Him, but woe to that man by whom He is betrayed! It would be better for him if he had not been born.”

Mark 14:22.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:22.text: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to the disciples, saying, “Take it; this is My body.”

Mark 14:24.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:24.text: He said to them, “This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.

Mark 14:25.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:25.text: Truly I tell you, I will no longer drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it anew in the kingdom of God.”

Mark 14:27.speaker: Jesus
