Mark 14:27.text: Then Jesus said to them, “You will all fall away, for it is written: ‘I will strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’

Mark 14:28.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:28.text: But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”

Mark 14:30.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:30.text: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “this very night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.”

Mark 14:32.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:32.text: Then they came to a place called Gethsemane, and Jesus told His disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”

Mark 14:34.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:34.text: Then He said to them, “My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch.”

Mark 14:36.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:36.text: “Abba, Father,” He said, “all things are possible for You. Take this cup from Me. Yet not what I will, but what You will.”

Mark 14:37.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:37.text: Then Jesus returned and found them sleeping. “Simon, are you asleep?” He asked. “Were you not able to keep watch for one hour?

Mark 14:38.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:38.text: Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation. For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.”

Mark 14:41.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:41.text: When Jesus returned the third time, He said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? That is enough! The hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

Mark 14:42.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:42.text: Rise, let us go. See, My betrayer is approaching!”

Mark 14:44.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:44.text: Now the betrayer had arranged a signal with them: “The One I kiss is the man; arrest Him and lead Him away securely.”

Mark 14:45.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:45.text: Going directly to Jesus, he said, “Rabbi!” and kissed Him.

Mark 14:48.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:48.text: Jesus asked the crowd, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me as you would an outlaw?

Mark 14:49.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:49.text: Every day I was with you, teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest Me. But this has happened that the Scriptures would be fulfilled.”

Mark 14:60.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:60.text: So the high priest stood up before them and questioned Jesus, “Have You no answer? What are these men testifying against You?”

Mark 14:61.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:61.text: But Jesus remained silent and made no reply. Again the high priest questioned Him, “Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”

Mark 14:62.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:62.text: “I am,” said Jesus, “and you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”

Mark 14:72.speaker: Jesus
Mark 14:72.text: And immediately the rooster crowed a second time. Then Peter remembered the word that Jesus had spoken to him: “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.” And he broke down and wept.

Mark 15:2.speaker: Jesus
Mark 15:2.text: So Pilate questioned Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?” “You have said so,” Jesus replied.

Mark 15:4.speaker: Jesus
Mark 15:4.text: Then Pilate questioned Him again, “Have You no answer? Look how many charges they are bringing against You!”

Mark 15:18.speaker: Jesus
Mark 15:18.text: And they began to salute Him: “Hail, King of the Jews!”

Mark 15:29.speaker: Jesus
Mark 15:29.text: And those who passed by heaped abuse on Him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days,

Mark 15:30.speaker: Jesus
Mark 15:30.text: come down from the cross and save Yourself!”

Mark 15:31.speaker: Jesus
Mark 15:31.text: In the same way, the chief priests and scribes mocked Him among themselves, saying, “He saved others, but He cannot save Himself!

Mark 15:32.speaker: Jesus
Mark 15:32.text: Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe!” And even those who were crucified with Him berated Him.

Mark 15:34.speaker: Jesus
Mark 15:34.text: At the ninth hour, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”

Mark 15:36.speaker: Jesus
Mark 15:36.text: And someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine. He put it on a reed and held it up for Jesus to drink, saying, “Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to take Him down.”

Mark 15:39.speaker: Jesus
Mark 15:39.text: When the centurion standing there in front of Jesus saw how He had breathed His last, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!”

Mark 16:3.speaker: Jesus
Mark 16:3.text: They were asking one another, “Who will roll away the stone from the entrance of the tomb?”

Mark 16:6.speaker: Jesus
Mark 16:6.text: But he said to them, “Do not be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified. He has risen! He is not here! See the place where they put Him.

Mark 16:7.speaker: Jesus
Mark 16:7.text: But go, tell His disciples and Peter, ‘He is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see Him, just as He told you.’”

Mark 16:15.speaker: Jesus
Mark 16:15.text: And He said to them, “Go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature.

Mark 16:16.speaker: Jesus
Mark 16:16.text: Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned.

Mark 16:17.speaker: Jesus
Mark 16:17.text: And these signs will accompany those who believe: In My name they will drive out demons; they will speak in new tongues;

Mark 16:18.speaker: Jesus
Mark 16:18.text: they will pick up snakes with their hands, and if they drink any deadly poison, it will not harm them; they will lay their hands on the sick, and they will be made well.”

Luke 2:23.speaker: Jesus
Luke 2:23.text: (as it is written in the Law of the Lord: “Every firstborn male shall be consecrated to the Lord”),

Luke 2:24.speaker: Jesus
Luke 2:24.text: and to offer the sacrifice specified in the Law of the Lord: “A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”

Luke 2:29.speaker: Jesus
Luke 2:29.text: “Sovereign Lord, as You have promised, You now dismiss Your servant in peace.

Luke 2:30.speaker: Jesus
Luke 2:30.text: For my eyes have seen Your salvation,

Luke 2:31.speaker: Jesus
Luke 2:31.text: which You have prepared in the sight of all people,

Luke 2:32.speaker: Jesus
Luke 2:32.text: a light for revelation to the Gentiles, and for glory to Your people Israel.”

Luke 3:4.speaker: Jesus
Luke 3:4.text: as it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet: “A voice of one calling in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him.

Luke 3:5.speaker: Jesus
Luke 3:5.text: Every valley shall be filled in, and every mountain and hill made low. The crooked ways shall be made straight, and the rough ways smooth.

Luke 3:6.speaker: Jesus
Luke 3:6.text: And all humanity will see God’s salvation.’”

Luke 3:22.speaker: Jesus
Luke 3:22.text: and the Holy Spirit descended on Him in a bodily form like a dove. And a voice came from heaven: “You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased.”

Luke 4:4.speaker: Jesus
Luke 4:4.text: But Jesus answered, “It is written: ‘Man shall not live on bread alone.’”

Luke 4:6.speaker: Jesus
Luke 4:6.text: “I will give You authority over all these kingdoms and all their glory,” he said. “For it has been relinquished to me, and I can give it to anyone I wish.

Luke 4:7.speaker: Jesus
Luke 4:7.text: So if You worship me, it will all be Yours.”

Luke 4:8.speaker: Jesus
Luke 4:8.text: But Jesus answered, “It is written: ‘Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only.’”

Luke 4:9.speaker: Jesus
Luke 4:9.text: Then the devil led Him to Jerusalem and set Him on the pinnacle of the temple. “If You are the Son of God,” he said, “throw Yourself down from here.

Luke 4:10.speaker: Jesus
Luke 4:10.text: For it is written: ‘He will command His angels concerning You to guard You carefully,

Luke 4:11.speaker: Jesus
Luke 4:11.text: and they will lift You up in their hands, so that You will not strike Your foot against a stone.’”

Luke 4:12.speaker: Jesus
Luke 4:12.text: But Jesus answered, “It also says, ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’”

Luke 4:18.speaker: Jesus
Luke 4:18.text: “The Spirit of the Lord is on Me, because He has anointed Me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent Me to proclaim liberty to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to release the oppressed,

Luke 4:19.speaker: Jesus
Luke 4:19.text: to proclaim the year of the Lord’s favor.”

Luke 4:21.speaker: Jesus
Luke 4:21.text: and He began by saying, “Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing.”

Luke 4:23.speaker: Jesus
Luke 4:23.text: Jesus said to them, “Surely you will quote this proverb to Me: ‘Physician, heal yourself! Do here in Your hometown what we have heard that You did in Capernaum.’”

Luke 4:24.speaker: Jesus
Luke 4:24.text: Then He added, “Truly I tell you, no prophet is accepted in his hometown.

Luke 4:25.speaker: Jesus
Luke 4:25.text: But I tell you truthfully that there were many widows in Israel in the time of Elijah, when the sky was shut for three and a half years and great famine swept over all the land.

Luke 4:26.speaker: Jesus
Luke 4:26.text: Yet Elijah was not sent to any of them, but to the widow of Zarephath in Sidon.

Luke 4:27.speaker: Jesus
Luke 4:27.text: And there were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet. Yet not one of them was cleansed—only Naaman the Syrian.”

Luke 4:34.speaker: Jesus
Luke 4:34.text: “Ha! What do You want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have You come to destroy us? I know who You are—the Holy One of God!”

Luke 4:35.speaker: Jesus
Luke 4:35.text: But Jesus rebuked the demon. “Be silent!” He said. “Come out of him!” At this, the demon threw the man down before them all and came out without harming him.

Luke 4:41.speaker: Jesus
Luke 4:41.text: Demons also came out of many people, shouting, “You are the Son of God!” But He rebuked the demons and would not allow them to speak, because they knew He was the Christ.

Luke 4:43.speaker: Jesus
Luke 4:43.text: But Jesus told them, “I must preach the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns as well, because that is why I was sent.”

Luke 5:4.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:4.text: When Jesus had finished speaking, He said to Simon, “Put out into deep water and let down your nets for a catch.”

Luke 5:8.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:8.text: When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees. “Go away from me, Lord,” he said, “for I am a sinful man.”

Luke 5:10.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:10.text: and so were his partners James and John, the sons of Zebedee. “Do not be afraid,” Jesus said to Simon. “From now on you will catch men.”

Luke 5:12.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:12.text: While Jesus was in one of the towns, a man came along who was covered with leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell facedown and begged Him, “Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean.”

Luke 5:13.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:13.text: Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man. “I am willing,” He said. “Be clean!” And immediately the leprosy left him.

Luke 5:14.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:14.text: “Do not tell anyone,” Jesus instructed him. “But go, show yourself to the priest and present the offering Moses prescribed for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.”

Luke 5:20.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:20.text: When Jesus saw their faith, He said, “Friend, your sins are forgiven.”

Luke 5:21.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:21.text: But the scribes and Pharisees began thinking to themselves, “Who is this man who speaks blasphemy? Who can forgive sins but God alone?”

Luke 5:22.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:22.text: Knowing what they were thinking, Jesus replied, “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?

Luke 5:23.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:23.text: Which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?

Luke 5:24.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:24.text: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on the earth to forgive sins…” He said to the paralytic, “I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”

Luke 5:27.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:27.text: After this, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth. “Follow Me,” He told him,

Luke 5:30.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:30.text: But the Pharisees and their scribes complained to Jesus’ disciples, “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”

Luke 5:31.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:31.text: Jesus answered, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.

Luke 5:32.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:32.text: I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance.”

Luke 5:34.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:34.text: Jesus replied, “Can you make the guests of the bridegroom fast while He is with them?

Luke 5:35.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:35.text: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.”

Luke 5:36.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:36.text: He also told them a parable: “No one tears a piece of cloth from a new garment and sews it on an old one. If he does, he will tear the new garment as well, and the patch from the new will not match the old.

Luke 5:37.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:37.text: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the new wine will burst the skins, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined.

Luke 5:38.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:38.text: Instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins.

Luke 5:39.speaker: Jesus
Luke 5:39.text: And no one after drinking old wine wants new, for he says, ‘The old is better.’”

Luke 6:3.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:3.text: Jesus replied, “Have you not read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?

Luke 6:4.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:4.text: He entered the house of God, took the consecrated bread and gave it to his companions, and ate what is lawful only for the priests to eat.”

Luke 6:5.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:5.text: Then Jesus declared, “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”

Luke 6:8.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:8.text: But Jesus knew their thoughts and said to the man with the withered hand, “Get up and stand among us.” So he got up and stood there.

Luke 6:9.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:9.text: Then Jesus said to them, “I ask you, which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?”

Luke 6:10.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:10.text: And after looking around at all of them, He said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did so, and it was restored.

Luke 6:20.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:20.text: Looking up at His disciples, Jesus said: “Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.

Luke 6:21.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:21.text: Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.

Luke 6:22.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:22.text: Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you and insult you and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man.

Luke 6:23.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:23.text: Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, because great is your reward in heaven. For their fathers treated the prophets in the same way.

Luke 6:24.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:24.text: But woe to you who are rich, for you have already received your comfort.

Luke 6:25.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:25.text: Woe to you who are well fed now, for you will hunger. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.

Luke 6:26.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:26.text: Woe to you when all men speak well of you, for their fathers treated the false prophets in the same way.

Luke 6:27.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:27.text: But to those of you who will listen, I say: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,

Luke 6:28.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:28.text: bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.

Luke 6:29.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:29.text: If someone strikes you on one cheek, turn to him the other also. And if someone takes your cloak, do not withhold your tunic as well.

Luke 6:30.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:30.text: Give to everyone who asks you, and if anyone takes what is yours, do not demand it back.

Luke 6:31.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:31.text: Do to others as you would have them do to you.

Luke 6:32.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:32.text: If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love those who love them.

Luke 6:33.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:33.text: If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do the same.

Luke 6:34.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:34.text: And if you lend to those from whom you expect repayment, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, expecting to be repaid in full.

Luke 6:35.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:35.text: But love your enemies, do good to them, and lend to them, expecting nothing in return. Then your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High; for He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked.

Luke 6:36.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:36.text: Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.

Luke 6:37.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:37.text: Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.

Luke 6:38.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:38.text: Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over will be poured into your lap. For with the measure you use, it will be measured back to you.”

Luke 6:39.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:39.text: Jesus also told them a parable: “Can a blind man lead a blind man? Will they not both fall into a pit?

Luke 6:40.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:40.text: A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher.

Luke 6:41.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:41.text: Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?

Luke 6:42.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:42.text: How can you say, ‘Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,’ while you yourself fail to see the beam in your own eye? You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.

Luke 6:43.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:43.text: No good tree bears bad fruit, nor does a bad tree bear good fruit.

Luke 6:44.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:44.text: For each tree is known by its own fruit. Indeed, figs are not gathered from thornbushes, nor grapes from brambles.

Luke 6:45.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:45.text: The good man brings good things out of the good treasure of his heart, and the evil man brings evil things out of the evil treasure of his heart. For out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks.

Luke 6:46.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:46.text: Why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord,’ but do not do what I say?

Luke 6:47.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:47.text: I will show you what he is like who comes to Me and hears My words and acts on them:

Luke 6:48.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:48.text: He is like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid his foundation on the rock. When the flood came, the torrent crashed against that house but could not shake it, because it was well built.

Luke 6:49.speaker: Jesus
Luke 6:49.text: But the one who hears My words and does not act on them is like a man who built his house on ground without a foundation. The torrent crashed against that house, and immediately it fell—and great was its destruction!”

Luke 7:4.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:4.text: They came to Jesus and pleaded with Him earnestly, “This man is worthy to have You grant this,

Luke 7:5.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:5.text: for he loves our nation and has built our synagogue.”

Luke 7:6.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:6.text: So Jesus went with them. But when He was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends with the message: “Lord, do not trouble Yourself, for I am not worthy to have You come under my roof.

Luke 7:7.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:7.text: That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to You. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.

Luke 7:8.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:8.text: For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one to go, and he goes, and another to come, and he comes. I tell my servant to do something, and he does it.”

Luke 7:9.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:9.text: When Jesus heard this, He marveled at the centurion. Turning to the crowd following Him, He said, “I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith.”

Luke 7:14.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:14.text: Then He went up and touched the coffin, and those carrying it stood still. “Young man,” He said, “I tell you, get up!”

Luke 7:19.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:19.text: So John called two of his disciples and sent them to ask the Lord, “Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?”

Luke 7:20.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:20.text: When the men came to Jesus, they said, “John the Baptist sent us to ask, ‘Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?’”

Luke 7:22.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:22.text: So He replied, “Go back and report to John what you have seen and heard: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor.

Luke 7:23.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:23.text: Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me.”

Luke 7:24.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:24.text: After John’s messengers had left, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swaying in the wind?

Luke 7:25.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:25.text: Otherwise, what did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? Look, those who wear elegant clothing and live in luxury are found in palaces.

Luke 7:26.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:26.text: What then did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.

Luke 7:27.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:27.text: This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You.’

Luke 7:28.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:28.text: I tell you, among those born of women there is no one greater than John, yet even the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.”

Luke 7:31.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:31.text: “To what, then, can I compare the men of this generation? What are they like?

Luke 7:32.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:32.text: They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling out to one another: ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not weep.’

Luke 7:33.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:33.text: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon!’

Luke 7:34.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:34.text: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’

Luke 7:35.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:35.text: But wisdom is vindicated by all her children.”

Luke 7:39.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:39.text: When the Pharisee who had invited Jesus saw this, he said to himself, “If this man were a prophet, He would know who this is and what kind of woman is touching Him—for she is a sinner!”

Luke 7:40.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:40.text: But Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” “Tell me, Teacher,” he said.

Luke 7:41.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:41.text: “Two men were debtors to a certain moneylender. One owed him five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.

Luke 7:42.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:42.text: When they were unable to repay him, he forgave both of them. Which one, then, will love him more?”

Luke 7:43.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:43.text: “I suppose the one who was forgiven more,” Simon replied. “You have judged correctly,” Jesus said.

Luke 7:44.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:44.text: And turning toward the woman, He said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? When I entered your house, you did not give Me water for My feet, but she wet My feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.

Luke 7:45.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:45.text: You did not greet Me with a kiss, but she has not stopped kissing My feet since I arrived.

Luke 7:46.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:46.text: You did not anoint My head with oil, but she has anointed My feet with perfume.

Luke 7:47.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:47.text: Therefore I tell you, her many sins have been forgiven, for she has loved much. But he who has been forgiven little loves little.”

Luke 7:48.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:48.text: Then Jesus said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”

Luke 7:50.speaker: Jesus
Luke 7:50.text: And Jesus told the woman, “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”

Luke 8:5.speaker: Jesus
Luke 8:5.text: “A farmer went out to sow his seed. And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, where it was trampled, and the birds of the air devoured it.

Luke 8:6.speaker: Jesus
Luke 8:6.text: Some fell on rocky ground, and when it came up, the seedlings withered because they had no moisture.

Luke 8:7.speaker: Jesus
Luke 8:7.text: Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up with it and choked the seedlings.

Luke 8:8.speaker: Jesus
Luke 8:8.text: Still other seed fell on good soil, where it sprang up and produced a crop—a hundredfold.” As Jesus said this, He called out, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”

Luke 8:20.speaker: Jesus
Luke 8:20.text: He was told, “Your mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to see You.”

Luke 8:21.speaker: Jesus
Luke 8:21.text: But He replied, “My mother and brothers are those who hear the word of God and carry it out.”

Luke 8:22.speaker: Jesus
Luke 8:22.text: One day Jesus said to His disciples, “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.” So He got into a boat with them and set out.

Luke 8:24.speaker: Jesus
Luke 8:24.text: The disciples went and woke Him, saying, “Master, Master, we are perishing!” Then Jesus got up and rebuked the wind and the raging waters, and they subsided, and all was calm.

Luke 8:25.speaker: Jesus
Luke 8:25.text: “Where is your faith?” He asked. Frightened and amazed, they asked one another, “Who is this? He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey Him!”

Luke 8:28.speaker: Jesus
Luke 8:28.text: When the man saw Jesus, he cried out and fell down before Him, shouting in a loud voice, “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You not to torture me!”

Luke 8:30.speaker: Jesus
Luke 8:30.text: “What is your name?” Jesus asked. “Legion,” he replied, because many demons had gone into him.

Luke 8:39.speaker: Jesus
Luke 8:39.text: “Return home and describe how much God has done for you.” So the man went away and proclaimed all over the town how much Jesus had done for him.

Luke 8:45.speaker: Jesus
Luke 8:45.text: “Who touched Me?” Jesus asked. But they all denied it. “Master,” said Peter, “the people are crowding and pressing against You.”

Luke 8:46.speaker: Jesus
Luke 8:46.text: But Jesus declared, “Someone touched Me, for I know that power has gone out from Me.”

Luke 8:48.speaker: Jesus
Luke 8:48.text: “Daughter,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you. Go in peace.”

Luke 8:49.speaker: Jesus
Luke 8:49.text: While He was still speaking, someone arrived from the house of the synagogue leader. “Your daughter is dead,” he told Jairus. “Do not bother the Teacher anymore.”

Luke 8:50.speaker: Jesus
Luke 8:50.text: But Jesus overheard them and said to Jairus, “Do not be afraid; just believe, and she will be healed.”

Luke 8:52.speaker: Jesus
Luke 8:52.text: Meanwhile, everyone was weeping and mourning for her. But Jesus said, “Stop weeping; she is not dead but asleep.”

Luke 8:54.speaker: Jesus
Luke 8:54.text: But Jesus took her by the hand and called out, “Child, get up!”

Luke 9:3.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:3.text: “Take nothing for the journey,” He told them, “no staff, no bag, no bread, no money, no second tunic.

Luke 9:4.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:4.text: Whatever house you enter, stay there until you leave that area.

Luke 9:5.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:5.text: If anyone does not welcome you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that town, as a testimony against them.”

Luke 9:9.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:9.text: “I beheaded John,” Herod said, “but who is this man I hear such things about?” And he kept trying to see Jesus.

Luke 9:12.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:12.text: As the day neared its end, the Twelve came to Jesus and said, “Dismiss the crowd so they can go to the surrounding villages and countryside for lodging and provisions. For we are in a desolate place here.”

Luke 9:13.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:13.text: But Jesus told them, “You give them something to eat.” “We have only five loaves of bread and two fish,” they answered, “unless we go and buy food for all these people.”

Luke 9:14.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:14.text: (There were about five thousand men.) He told His disciples, “Have them sit down in groups of about fifty each.”

Luke 9:18.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:18.text: One day as Jesus was praying in private and the disciples were with Him, He questioned them: “Who do the crowds say I am?”

Luke 9:20.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:20.text: “But what about you?” Jesus asked. “Who do you say I am?” Peter answered, “The Christ of God.”

Luke 9:22.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:22.text: “The Son of Man must suffer many things,” He said. “He must be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and He must be killed and on the third day be raised to life.”

Luke 9:23.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:23.text: Then Jesus said to all of them, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow Me.

Luke 9:24.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:24.text: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake will save it.

Luke 9:25.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:25.text: What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet lose or forfeit his very self?

Luke 9:26.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:26.text: If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him when He comes in His glory and in the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.

Luke 9:27.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:27.text: But I tell you truly, some who are standing here will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God.”

Luke 9:33.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:33.text: As Moses and Elijah were leaving, Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it is good for us to be here. Let us put up three shelters—one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” (He did not know what he was saying.)

Luke 9:35.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:35.text: And a voice came from the cloud, saying, “This is My Son, whom I have chosen. Listen to Him!”

Luke 9:41.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:41.text: “O unbelieving and perverse generation!” Jesus replied. “How long must I remain with you and put up with you? Bring your son here.”

Luke 9:44.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:44.text: “Let these words sink into your ears: The Son of Man is about to be delivered into the hands of men.”

Luke 9:48.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:48.text: And He said to them, “Whoever welcomes this little child in My name welcomes Me, and whoever welcomes Me welcomes the One who sent Me. For whoever is the least among all of you, he is the greatest.”

Luke 9:50.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:50.text: “Do not stop him,” Jesus replied, “for whoever is not against you is for you.”

Luke 9:57.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:57.text: As they were walking along the road, someone said to Jesus, “I will follow You wherever You go.”

Luke 9:58.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:58.text: Jesus replied, “Foxes have dens and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.”

Luke 9:59.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:59.text: Then He said to another man, “Follow Me.” The man replied, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.”

Luke 9:60.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:60.text: But Jesus told him, “Let the dead bury their own dead. You, however, go and proclaim the kingdom of God.”

Luke 9:62.speaker: Jesus
Luke 9:62.text: Then Jesus declared, “No one who puts his hand to the plow and then looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”

Luke 10:2.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:2.text: And He told them, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few. Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest.

Luke 10:3.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:3.text: Go! I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.

Luke 10:4.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:4.text: Carry no purse or bag or sandals. Do not greet anyone along the road.

Luke 10:5.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:5.text: Whatever house you enter, begin by saying, ‘Peace to this house.’

Luke 10:6.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:6.text: If a man of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; if not, it will return to you.

Luke 10:7.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:7.text: Stay at the same house, eating and drinking whatever you are offered. For the worker is worthy of his wages. Do not move around from house to house.

Luke 10:8.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:8.text: If you enter a town and they welcome you, eat whatever is set before you.

Luke 10:9.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:9.text: Heal the sick who are there and tell them, ‘The kingdom of God is near you.’

Luke 10:10.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:10.text: But if you enter a town and they do not welcome you, go into the streets and declare,

Luke 10:11.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:11.text: ‘Even the dust of your town that clings to our feet, we wipe off as a testimony against you. Yet be sure of this: The kingdom of God is near.’

Luke 10:12.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:12.text: I tell you, it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom than for that town.

Luke 10:13.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:13.text: Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.

Luke 10:14.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:14.text: But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you.

Luke 10:15.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:15.text: And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will be brought down to Hades!

Luke 10:16.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:16.text: Whoever listens to you listens to Me; whoever rejects you rejects Me; and whoever rejects Me rejects the One who sent Me.”

Luke 10:21.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:21.text: At that time Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and declared, “I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight.

Luke 10:22.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:22.text: All things have been entrusted to Me by My Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, and no one knows who the Father is except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.”

Luke 10:23.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:23.text: Then Jesus turned to the disciples and said privately, “Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.

Luke 10:24.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:24.text: For I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.”

Luke 10:25.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:25.text: One day an expert in the law stood up to test Him. “Teacher,” he asked, “what must I do to inherit eternal life?”

Luke 10:26.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:26.text: “What is written in the Law?” Jesus replied. “How do you read it?”

Luke 10:27.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:27.text: He answered, “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind’ and ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’”

Luke 10:28.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:28.text: “You have answered correctly,” Jesus said. “Do this and you will live.”

Luke 10:29.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:29.text: But wanting to justify himself, he asked Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”

Luke 10:30.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:30.text: Jesus took up this question and said, “A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho when he fell into the hands of robbers. They stripped him, beat him, and went away, leaving him half dead.

Luke 10:31.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:31.text: Now by chance a priest was going down the same road, but when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.

Luke 10:32.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:32.text: So too, when a Levite came to that spot and saw him, he passed by on the other side.

Luke 10:33.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:33.text: But a Samaritan on a journey came upon him, and when he saw him, he had compassion.

Luke 10:34.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:34.text: He went to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. Then he put him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.

Luke 10:35.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:35.text: The next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper. ‘Take care of him,’ he said, ‘and on my return I will repay you for any additional expense.’

Luke 10:36.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:36.text: Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of robbers?”

Luke 10:37.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:37.text: “The one who showed him mercy,” replied the expert in the law. Then Jesus told him, “Go and do likewise.”

Luke 10:40.speaker: Jesus
Luke 10:40.text: But Martha was distracted by all the preparations to be made. She came to Jesus and said, “Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her to help me!”

Luke 11:1.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:1.text: One day in a place where Jesus had just finished praying, one of His disciples requested, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John taught his disciples.”

Luke 11:2.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:2.text: So Jesus told them, “When you pray, say: ‘Father, hallowed be Your name. Your kingdom come.

Luke 11:3.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:3.text: Give us each day our daily bread.

Luke 11:4.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:4.text: And forgive us our sins, for we also forgive everyone who sins against us. And lead us not into temptation.’”

Luke 11:5.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:5.text: Then Jesus said to them, “Suppose one of you goes to his friend at midnight and says, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,

Luke 11:6.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:6.text: because a friend of mine has come to me on a journey, and I have nothing to set before him.’

Luke 11:7.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:7.text: And suppose the one inside answers, ‘Do not bother me. My door is already shut, and my children and I are in bed. I cannot get up to give you anything.’

Luke 11:8.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:8.text: I tell you, even though he will not get up to provide for him because of his friendship, yet because of the man’s persistence, he will get up and give him as much as he needs.

Luke 11:9.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:9.text: So I tell you: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.

Luke 11:10.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:10.text: For everyone who asks receives; he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened.

Luke 11:11.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:11.text: What father among you, if his son asks for a fish, will give him a snake instead?

Luke 11:12.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:12.text: Or if he asks for an egg, will give him a scorpion?

Luke 11:13.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:13.text: So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!”

Luke 11:17.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:17.text: Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and a house divided against a house will fall.

Luke 11:18.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:18.text: If Satan is divided against himself, how can his kingdom stand? After all, you say that I drive out demons by Beelzebul.

Luke 11:19.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:19.text: And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? So then, they will be your judges.

Luke 11:20.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:20.text: But if I drive out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.

Luke 11:21.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:21.text: When a strong man, fully armed, guards his house, his possessions are secure.

Luke 11:22.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:22.text: But when someone stronger attacks and overpowers him, he takes away the armor in which the man trusted, and then he divides up his plunder.

Luke 11:23.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:23.text: He who is not with Me is against Me, and he who does not gather with Me scatters.

Luke 11:24.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:24.text: When an unclean spirit comes out of a man, it passes through arid places seeking rest and does not find it. Then it says, ‘I will return to the house I left.’

Luke 11:25.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:25.text: On its return, it finds the house swept clean and put in order.

Luke 11:26.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:26.text: Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in and dwell there. And the final plight of that man is worse than the first.”

Luke 11:28.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:28.text: But He replied, “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it.”

Luke 11:29.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:29.text: As the crowds were increasing, Jesus said, “This is a wicked generation. It demands a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of Jonah.

Luke 11:30.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:30.text: For as Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation.

Luke 11:31.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:31.text: The Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them; for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and now One greater than Solomon is here.

Luke 11:32.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:32.text: The men of Nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and now One greater than Jonah is here.

Luke 11:33.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:33.text: No one lights a lamp and puts it in a cellar or under a basket. Instead, he sets it on a stand, so those who enter can see the light.

Luke 11:34.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:34.text: Your eye is the lamp of your body. When your eyes are good, your whole body also is full of light. But when they are bad, your body is full of darkness.

Luke 11:35.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:35.text: Be careful, then, that the light within you is not darkness.

Luke 11:36.speaker: Jesus
Luke 11:36.text: So if your whole body is full of light, with no part of it in darkness, you will be radiant, as though a lamp were shining on you.”

Luke 12:1.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:1.text: In the meantime, a crowd of many thousands had gathered, so that they were trampling one another. Jesus began to speak first to His disciples: “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

Luke 12:2.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:2.text: There is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.

Luke 12:3.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:3.text: What you have spoken in the dark will be heard in the daylight, and what you have whispered in the inner rooms will be proclaimed from the housetops.

Luke 12:4.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:4.text: I tell you, My friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do no more.

Luke 12:5.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:5.text: But I will show you whom you should fear: Fear the One who, after you have been killed, has authority to throw you into hell. Yes, I tell you, fear Him!

Luke 12:6.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:6.text: Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? Yet not one of them is forgotten by God.

Luke 12:7.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:7.text: And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.

Luke 12:8.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:8.text: I tell you, everyone who confesses Me before men, the Son of Man will also confess him before the angels of God.

Luke 12:9.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:9.text: But whoever denies Me before men will be denied before the angels of God.

Luke 12:10.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:10.text: And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.

Luke 12:11.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:11.text: When you are brought before synagogues, rulers, and authorities, do not worry about how to defend yourselves or what to say.

Luke 12:12.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:12.text: For at that time the Holy Spirit will teach you what you should say.”

Luke 12:14.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:14.text: But Jesus replied, “Man, who appointed Me judge or executor between you?”

Luke 12:15.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:15.text: And He said to them, “Watch out! Guard yourselves against every form of greed, for one’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.”

Luke 12:16.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:16.text: Then He told them a parable: “The ground of a certain rich man produced an abundance.

Luke 12:17.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:17.text: So he thought to himself, ‘What shall I do, since I have nowhere to store my crops?’

Luke 12:18.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:18.text: Then he said, ‘This is what I will do: I will tear down my barns and will build bigger ones, and there I will store up all my grain and my goods.

Luke 12:19.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:19.text: Then I will say to myself, “You have plenty of good things laid up for many years. Take it easy. Eat, drink, and be merry!”’

Luke 12:20.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:20.text: But God said to him, ‘You fool! This very night your life will be required of you. Then who will own what you have accumulated?’

Luke 12:21.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:21.text: This is how it will be for anyone who stores up treasure for himself but is not rich toward God.”

Luke 12:22.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:22.text: Then Jesus said to His disciples, “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.

Luke 12:23.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:23.text: For life is more than food, and the body more than clothes.

Luke 12:24.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:24.text: Consider the ravens: They do not sow or reap, they have no storehouse or barn; yet God feeds them. How much more valuable you are than the birds!

Luke 12:25.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:25.text: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?

Luke 12:26.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:26.text: So if you cannot do such a small thing, why do you worry about the rest?

Luke 12:27.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:27.text: Consider how the lilies grow: They do not labor or spin. Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.

Luke 12:28.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:28.text: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, how much more will He clothe you, O you of little faith!

Luke 12:29.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:29.text: And do not be concerned about what you will eat or drink. Do not worry about it.

Luke 12:30.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:30.text: For the Gentiles of the world strive after all these things, and your Father knows that you need them.

Luke 12:31.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:31.text: But seek His kingdom, and these things will be added unto you.

Luke 12:32.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:32.text: Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.

Luke 12:33.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:33.text: Sell your possessions and give to the poor. Provide yourselves with purses that will not wear out, an inexhaustible treasure in heaven, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.

Luke 12:34.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:34.text: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

Luke 12:35.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:35.text: Be dressed for service and keep your lamps burning.

Luke 12:36.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:36.text: Then you will be like servants waiting for their master to return from the wedding banquet, so that when he comes and knocks, they can open the door for him at once.

Luke 12:37.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:37.text: Blessed are those servants whom the master finds on watch when he returns. Truly I tell you, he will dress himself to serve and will have them recline at the table, and he himself will come and wait on them.

Luke 12:38.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:38.text: Even if he comes in the second or third watch of the night and finds them alert, those servants will be blessed.

Luke 12:39.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:39.text: But understand this: If the homeowner had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be broken into.

Luke 12:40.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:40.text: You also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.”

Luke 12:54.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:54.text: Then Jesus said to the crowds, “As soon as you see a cloud rising in the west, you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and that is what happens.

Luke 12:55.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:55.text: And when the south wind blows, you say, ‘It will be hot,’ and it is.

Luke 12:56.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:56.text: You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and sky. Why don’t you know how to interpret the present time?

Luke 12:57.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:57.text: And why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right?

Luke 12:58.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:58.text: Make every effort to reconcile with your adversary while you are on your way to the magistrate. Otherwise, he may drag you off to the judge, and the judge may hand you over to the officer, and the officer may throw you into prison.

Luke 12:59.speaker: Jesus
Luke 12:59.text: I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the very last penny.”

Luke 13:2.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:2.text: To this He replied, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered this way?

Luke 13:3.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:3.text: No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish.

Luke 13:4.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:4.text: Or those eighteen who were killed when the tower of Siloam collapsed on them: Do you think that they were more sinful than all the others living in Jerusalem?

Luke 13:5.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:5.text: No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish.”

Luke 13:6.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:6.text: Then Jesus told this parable: “A man had a fig tree that was planted in his vineyard. He went to look for fruit on it but did not find any.

Luke 13:7.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:7.text: So he said to the keeper of the vineyard, ‘Look, for the past three years I have come to search for fruit on this fig tree and haven’t found any. Therefore cut it down! Why should it use up the soil?’

Luke 13:8.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:8.text: ‘Sir,’ the man replied, ‘leave it alone again this year, until I dig around it and fertilize it.

Luke 13:9.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:9.text: If it bears fruit next year, fine. But if not, you can cut it down.’”

Luke 13:12.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:12.text: When Jesus saw her, He called her over and said, “Woman, you are set free from your disability.”

Luke 13:14.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:14.text: But the synagogue leader was indignant that Jesus had healed on the Sabbath. “There are six days for work,” he told the crowd. “So come and be healed on those days and not on the Sabbath.”

Luke 13:18.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:18.text: Then Jesus asked, “What is the kingdom of God like? To what can I compare it?

Luke 13:19.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:19.text: It is like a mustard seed that a man tossed into his garden. It grew and became a tree, and the birds of the air nested in its branches.”

Luke 13:20.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:20.text: Again He asked, “To what can I compare the kingdom of God?

Luke 13:21.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:21.text: It is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened.”

Luke 13:23.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:23.text: “Lord,” someone asked Him, “will only a few people be saved?” Jesus answered,

Luke 13:24.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:24.text: “Make every effort to enter through the narrow door. For many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able.

Luke 13:25.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:25.text: After the master of the house gets up and shuts the door, you will stand outside knocking and saying, ‘Lord, open the door for us.’ But he will reply, ‘I do not know where you are from.’

Luke 13:26.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:26.text: Then you will say, ‘We ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets.’

Luke 13:27.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:27.text: And he will answer, ‘I tell you, I do not know where you are from. Depart from me, all you evildoers.’

Luke 13:28.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:28.text: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but you yourselves are thrown out.

Luke 13:29.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:29.text: People will come from east and west and north and south, and will recline at the table in the kingdom of God.

Luke 13:30.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:30.text: And indeed, some who are last will be first, and some who are first will be last.”

Luke 13:31.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:31.text: At that very hour, some Pharisees came to Jesus and told Him, “Leave this place and get away, because Herod wants to kill You.”

Luke 13:32.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:32.text: But Jesus replied, “Go tell that fox, ‘Look, I will keep driving out demons and healing people today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will reach My goal.’

Luke 13:33.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:33.text: Nevertheless, I must keep going today and tomorrow and the next day, for it is not admissible for a prophet to perish outside of Jerusalem.

Luke 13:34.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:34.text: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I have longed to gather your children together as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!

Luke 13:35.speaker: Jesus
Luke 13:35.text: Look, your house is left to you desolate. And I tell you that you will not see Me again until you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.’”

Luke 14:3.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:3.text: So Jesus asked the experts in the law and the Pharisees, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath or not?”

Luke 14:5.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:5.text: And He asked them, “Which of you whose son or ox falls into a pit on the Sabbath day will not immediately pull him out?”

Luke 14:8.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:8.text: “When you are invited to a wedding banquet, do not sit in the place of honor, in case someone more distinguished than you has been invited.

Luke 14:9.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:9.text: Then the host who invited both of you will come and tell you, ‘Give this man your seat.’ And in humiliation, you will have to take the last place.

Luke 14:10.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:10.text: But when you are invited, go and sit in the last place, so that your host will come and tell you, ‘Friend, move up to a better place.’ Then you will be honored in front of everyone at the table with you.

Luke 14:11.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:11.text: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”

Luke 14:12.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:12.text: Then Jesus said to the man who had invited Him, “When you host a dinner or a banquet, do not invite your friends or brothers or relatives or rich neighbors. Otherwise, they may invite you in return, and you will be repaid.

Luke 14:13.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:13.text: But when you host a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind,

Luke 14:14.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:14.text: and you will be blessed. Since they cannot repay you, you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”

Luke 14:15.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:15.text: When one of those reclining with Him heard this, he said to Jesus, “Blessed is everyone who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of God.”

Luke 14:16.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:16.text: But Jesus replied, “A certain man prepared a great banquet and invited many guests.

Luke 14:17.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:17.text: When it was time for the banquet, he sent his servant to tell those who had been invited, ‘Come, for everything is now ready.’

Luke 14:18.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:18.text: But one after another they all began to make excuses. The first one said, ‘I have bought a field, and I need to go see it. Please excuse me.’

Luke 14:19.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:19.text: Another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out. Please excuse me.’

Luke 14:20.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:20.text: Still another said, ‘I have married a wife, so I cannot come.’

Luke 14:21.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:21.text: The servant returned and reported all this to his master. Then the owner of the house became angry and said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and alleys of the city, and bring in the poor, the crippled, the blind, and the lame.’

Luke 14:22.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:22.text: ‘Sir,’ the servant replied, ‘what you ordered has been done, and there is still room.’

Luke 14:23.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:23.text: So the master told his servant, ‘Go out to the highways and hedges and compel them to come in, so that my house will be full.

Luke 14:24.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:24.text: For I tell you, not one of those men who were invited will taste my banquet.’”

Luke 14:26.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:26.text: “If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters—yes, even his own life—he cannot be My disciple.

Luke 14:27.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:27.text: And whoever does not carry his cross and follow Me cannot be My disciple.

Luke 14:28.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:28.text: Which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost to see if he has the resources to complete it?

Luke 14:29.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:29.text: Otherwise, if he lays the foundation and is unable to finish the work, everyone who sees it will ridicule him,

Luke 14:30.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:30.text: saying, ‘This man could not finish what he started to build.’

Luke 14:31.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:31.text: Or what king on his way to war with another king will not first sit down and consider whether he can engage with ten thousand men the one coming against him with twenty thousand?

Luke 14:32.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:32.text: And if he is unable, he will send a delegation while the other king is still far off, to ask for terms of peace.

Luke 14:33.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:33.text: In the same way, any one of you who does not give up everything he has cannot be My disciple.

Luke 14:34.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:34.text: Salt is good, but if the salt loses its savor, with what will it be seasoned?

Luke 14:35.speaker: Jesus
Luke 14:35.text: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile, and it is thrown out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”

Luke 15:2.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:2.text: So the Pharisees and scribes began to grumble: “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.”

Luke 15:4.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:4.text: “What man among you, if he has a hundred sheep and loses one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the pasture and go after the one that is lost, until he finds it?

Luke 15:5.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:5.text: And when he finds it, he joyfully puts it on his shoulders,

Luke 15:6.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:6.text: comes home, and calls together his friends and neighbors to tell them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost sheep!’

Luke 15:7.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:7.text: I tell you that in the same way there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous ones who do not need to repent.

Luke 15:8.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:8.text: Or what woman who has ten silver coins and loses one of them does not light a lamp, sweep her house, and search carefully until she finds it?

Luke 15:9.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:9.text: And when she finds it, she calls together her friends and neighbors to say, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost coin.’

Luke 15:10.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:10.text: In the same way, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of God’s angels over one sinner who repents.”

Luke 15:11.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:11.text: Then Jesus said, “There was a man who had two sons.

Luke 15:12.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:12.text: The younger son said to him, ‘Father, give me my share of the estate.’ So he divided his property between them.

Luke 15:13.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:13.text: After a few days, the younger son got everything together and journeyed to a distant country, where he squandered his wealth in wild living.

Luke 15:14.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:14.text: After he had spent all he had, a severe famine swept through that country, and he began to be in need.

Luke 15:15.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:15.text: So he went and hired himself out to a citizen of that country, who sent him into his fields to feed the pigs.

Luke 15:16.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:16.text: He longed to fill his belly with the pods the pigs were eating, but no one would give him a thing.

Luke 15:17.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:17.text: Finally he came to his senses and said, ‘How many of my father’s hired servants have plenty of food, but here I am, starving to death!

Luke 15:18.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:18.text: I will get up and go back to my father and say to him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.

Luke 15:19.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:19.text: I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired servants.”’

Luke 15:20.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:20.text: So he got up and went to his father. But while he was still in the distance, his father saw him and was filled with compassion. He ran to his son, embraced him, and kissed him.

Luke 15:21.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:21.text: The son declared, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’

Luke 15:22.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:22.text: But the father said to his servants, ‘Quick! Bring the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.

Luke 15:23.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:23.text: Bring the fattened calf and kill it. Let us feast and celebrate.

Luke 15:24.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:24.text: For this son of mine was dead and is alive again! He was lost and is found!’ So they began to celebrate.

Luke 15:25.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:25.text: Meanwhile the older son was in the field, and as he approached the house, he heard music and dancing.

Luke 15:26.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:26.text: So he called one of the servants and asked what was going on.

Luke 15:27.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:27.text: ‘Your brother has returned,’ he said, ‘and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has him back safe and sound.’

Luke 15:28.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:28.text: The older son became angry and refused to go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.

Luke 15:29.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:29.text: But he answered his father, ‘Look, all these years I have served you and never disobeyed a commandment of yours. Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.

Luke 15:30.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:30.text: But when this son of yours returns from squandering your wealth with prostitutes, you kill the fattened calf for him!’

Luke 15:31.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:31.text: ‘Son, you are always with me,’ the father said, ‘and all that is mine is yours.

Luke 15:32.speaker: Jesus
Luke 15:32.text: But it was fitting to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’”

Luke 16:1.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:1.text: Jesus also said to His disciples, “There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his possessions.

Luke 16:2.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:2.text: So he called him in to ask, ‘What is this I hear about you? Turn in an account of your management, for you cannot be manager any longer.’

Luke 16:3.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:3.text: The manager said to himself, ‘What shall I do, now that my master is taking away my position? I am too weak to dig and too ashamed to beg.

Luke 16:4.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:4.text: I know what I will do so that after my removal from management, people will welcome me into their homes.’

Luke 16:5.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:5.text: And he called in each one of his master’s debtors. ‘How much do you owe my master?’ he asked the first.

Luke 16:6.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:6.text: ‘A hundred measures of olive oil,’ he answered. ‘Take your bill,’ said the manager, ‘sit down quickly, and write fifty.’

Luke 16:7.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:7.text: Then he asked another, ‘And how much do you owe?’ ‘A hundred measures of wheat,’ he replied. ‘Take your bill and write eighty,’ he told him.

Luke 16:8.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:8.text: The master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly. For the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the sons of light.

Luke 16:9.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:9.text: I tell you, use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves so that when it is gone, they will welcome you into eternal dwellings.

Luke 16:10.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:10.text: Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.

Luke 16:11.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:11.text: So if you have not been faithful with worldly wealth, who will entrust you with true riches?

Luke 16:12.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:12.text: And if you have not been faithful with the belongings of another, who will give you belongings of your own?

Luke 16:13.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:13.text: No servant can serve two masters. Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.”

Luke 16:15.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:15.text: So He said to them, “You are the ones who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts. For what is prized among men is detestable before God.

Luke 16:16.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:16.text: The Law and the Prophets were proclaimed until John. Since that time, the gospel of the kingdom of God is being preached, and everyone is forcing his way into it.

Luke 16:17.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:17.text: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for a single stroke of a pen to drop out of the Law.

Luke 16:18.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:18.text: Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery, and he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.

Luke 16:19.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:19.text: Now there was a rich man dressed in purple and fine linen, who lived each day in joyous splendor.

Luke 16:20.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:20.text: And a beggar named Lazarus lay at his gate, covered with sores

Luke 16:21.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:21.text: and longing to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.

Luke 16:22.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:22.text: One day the beggar died and was carried by the angels to Abraham’s side. And the rich man also died and was buried.

Luke 16:23.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:23.text: In Hades, where he was in torment, he looked up and saw Abraham from afar, with Lazarus by his side.

Luke 16:24.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:24.text: So he cried out, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue. For I am in agony in this fire.’

Luke 16:25.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:25.text: But Abraham answered, ‘Child, remember that during your lifetime you received your good things, while Lazarus received bad things. But now he is comforted here, while you are in agony.

Luke 16:26.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:26.text: And besides all this, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that even those who wish cannot cross from here to you, nor can anyone cross from there to us.’

Luke 16:27.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:27.text: ‘Then I beg you, father,’ he said, ‘send Lazarus to my father’s house,

Luke 16:28.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:28.text: for I have five brothers. Let him warn them, so that they will not also end up in this place of torment.’

Luke 16:29.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:29.text: But Abraham replied, ‘They have Moses and the Prophets; let your brothers listen to them.’

Luke 16:30.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:30.text: ‘No, father Abraham,’ he said, ‘but if someone is sent to them from the dead, they will repent.’

Luke 16:31.speaker: Jesus
Luke 16:31.text: Then Abraham said to him, ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead.’”

Luke 17:1.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:1.text: Jesus said to His disciples, “It is inevitable that stumbling blocks will come, but woe to the one through whom they come!

Luke 17:2.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:2.text: It would be better for him to have a millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea than to cause one of these little ones to stumble.

Luke 17:3.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:3.text: Watch yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.

Luke 17:4.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:4.text: Even if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times returns to say, ‘I repent,’ you must forgive him.”

Luke 17:13.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:13.text: and raised their voices, shouting, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”

Luke 17:14.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:14.text: When Jesus saw them, He said, “Go, show yourselves to the priests.” And as they were on their way, they were cleansed.

Luke 17:17.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:17.text: “Were not all ten cleansed?” Jesus asked. “Where then are the other nine?

Luke 17:18.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:18.text: Was no one found except this foreigner to return and give glory to God?”

Luke 17:19.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:19.text: Then Jesus said to him, “Rise and go; your faith has made you well!”

Luke 17:20.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:20.text: When asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God would come, Jesus replied, “The kingdom of God will not come with observable signs.

Luke 17:21.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:21.text: Nor will people say, ‘Look, here it is,’ or ‘There it is.’ For you see, the kingdom of God is in your midst.”

Luke 17:22.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:22.text: Then He said to the disciples, “The time is coming when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, but you will not see it.

Luke 17:23.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:23.text: People will tell you, ‘Look, there He is!’ or ‘Look, here He is!’ Do not go out or chase after them.

Luke 17:24.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:24.text: For just as the lightning flashes and lights up the sky from one end to the other, so will be the Son of Man in His day.

Luke 17:25.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:25.text: But first He must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.

Luke 17:26.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:26.text: Just as it was in the days of Noah, so also will it be in the days of the Son of Man:

Luke 17:27.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:27.text: People were eating and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark. Then the flood came and destroyed them all.

Luke 17:28.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:28.text: It was the same in the days of Lot: People were eating and drinking, buying and selling, planting and building.

Luke 17:29.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:29.text: But on the day Lot left Sodom, fire and sulfur rained down from heaven and destroyed them all.

Luke 17:30.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:30.text: It will be just like that on the day the Son of Man is revealed.

Luke 17:31.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:31.text: On that day, let no one on the housetop come down to retrieve his possessions. Likewise, let no one in the field return for anything he has left behind.

Luke 17:33.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:33.text: Whoever tries to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life will preserve it.

Luke 17:34.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:34.text: I tell you, on that night two people will be in one bed: one will be taken and the other left.

Luke 17:35.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:35.text: Two women will be grinding grain together: one will be taken and the other left.”

Luke 17:37.speaker: Jesus
Luke 17:37.text: “Where, Lord?” they asked. Jesus answered, “Wherever there is a carcass, there the vultures will gather.”

Luke 18:2.speaker: Jesus
Luke 18:2.text: “In a certain town there was a judge who neither feared God nor respected men.

Luke 18:3.speaker: Jesus
Luke 18:3.text: And there was a widow in that town who kept appealing to him, ‘Give me justice against my adversary.’

Luke 18:4.speaker: Jesus
Luke 18:4.text: For a while he refused, but later he said to himself, ‘Though I neither fear God nor respect men,

Luke 18:5.speaker: Jesus
Luke 18:5.text: yet because this widow keeps pestering me, I will give her justice. Otherwise, she will wear me out with her perpetual requests.’”

Luke 18:16.speaker: Jesus
Luke 18:16.text: But Jesus called the children to Him and said, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

Luke 18:17.speaker: Jesus
Luke 18:17.text: Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.”

Luke 18:19.speaker: Jesus
Luke 18:19.text: “Why do you call Me good?” Jesus replied. “No one is good except God alone.

Luke 18:20.speaker: Jesus
Luke 18:20.text: You know the commandments: ‘Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honor your father and mother.’”

Luke 18:21.speaker: Jesus
Luke 18:21.text: “All these I have kept from my youth,” he said.

Luke 18:22.speaker: Jesus
Luke 18:22.text: On hearing this, Jesus told him, “You still lack one thing: Sell everything you own and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”

Luke 18:24.speaker: Jesus
Luke 18:24.text: Seeing the man’s sadness, Jesus said, “How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!

Luke 18:25.speaker: Jesus
Luke 18:25.text: Indeed, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”

Luke 18:27.speaker: Jesus
Luke 18:27.text: But Jesus said, “What is impossible with man is possible with God.”

Luke 18:29.speaker: Jesus
Luke 18:29.text: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “no one who has left home or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God

Luke 18:30.speaker: Jesus
Luke 18:30.text: will fail to receive many times more in this age—and in the age to come, eternal life.”

Luke 18:31.speaker: Jesus
Luke 18:31.text: Then Jesus took the Twelve aside and said to them, “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything the prophets have written about the Son of Man will be fulfilled.

Luke 18:32.speaker: Jesus
Luke 18:32.text: He will be delivered over to the Gentiles and will be mocked and insulted and spit upon.

Luke 18:33.speaker: Jesus
Luke 18:33.text: They will flog Him and kill Him, and on the third day He will rise again.”

Luke 18:41.speaker: Jesus
Luke 18:41.text: “What do you want Me to do for you?” “Lord,” he said, “let me see again.”

Luke 18:42.speaker: Jesus
Luke 18:42.text: “Receive your sight!” Jesus replied. “Your faith has healed you.”

Luke 19:5.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:5.text: When Jesus came to that place, He looked up and said, “Zacchaeus, hurry down, for I must stay at your house today.”

Luke 19:7.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:7.text: And all who saw this began to grumble, saying, “He has gone to be the guest of a sinful man!”

Luke 19:9.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:9.text: Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, because this man too is a son of Abraham.

Luke 19:10.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:10.text: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.”

Luke 19:12.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:12.text: So He said, “A man of noble birth went to a distant country to lay claim to his kingship and then return.

Luke 19:13.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:13.text: Beforehand, he called ten of his servants and gave them ten minas. ‘Conduct business with this until I return,’ he said.

Luke 19:14.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:14.text: But his subjects hated him and sent a delegation after him to say, ‘We do not want this man to rule over us.’

Luke 19:15.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:15.text: When he returned from procuring his kingship, he summoned the servants to whom he had given the money, to find out what each one had earned.

Luke 19:16.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:16.text: The first servant came forward and said, ‘Master, your mina has produced ten more minas.’

Luke 19:17.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:17.text: His master replied, ‘Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in a very small matter, you shall have authority over ten cities.’

Luke 19:18.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:18.text: The second servant came and said, ‘Master, your mina has made five minas.’

Luke 19:19.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:19.text: And to this one he said, ‘You shall have authority over five cities.’

Luke 19:20.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:20.text: Then another servant came and said, ‘Master, here is your mina, which I have laid away in a piece of cloth.

Luke 19:21.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:21.text: For I was afraid of you, because you are a harsh man. You withdraw what you did not deposit and reap what you did not sow.’

Luke 19:22.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:22.text: His master replied, ‘You wicked servant, I will judge you by your own words. So you knew that I am a harsh man, withdrawing what I did not deposit and reaping what I did not sow?

Luke 19:23.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:23.text: Why then did you not deposit my money in the bank, and upon my return I could have collected it with interest?’

Luke 19:24.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:24.text: Then he told those standing by, ‘Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.’

Luke 19:26.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:26.text: He replied, ‘I tell you that everyone who has will be given more; but the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.

Luke 19:27.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:27.text: And these enemies of mine who were unwilling for me to rule over them, bring them here and slay them in front of me.’”

Luke 19:30.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:30.text: saying, “Go into the village ahead of you, and as you enter it, you will find a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it here.

Luke 19:31.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:31.text: If anyone asks, ‘Why are you untying it?’ tell him, ‘The Lord needs it.’”

Luke 19:38.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:38.text: “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord!” “Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!”

Luke 19:46.speaker: Jesus
Luke 19:46.text: He declared to them, “It is written: ‘My house will be a house of prayer.’ But you have made it ‘a den of robbers.’”

Luke 20:3.speaker: Jesus
Luke 20:3.text: “I will also ask you a question,” Jesus replied. “Tell Me:

Luke 20:4.speaker: Jesus
Luke 20:4.text: John’s baptism—was it from heaven, or from men?”

Luke 20:8.speaker: Jesus
Luke 20:8.text: And Jesus replied, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.”

Luke 20:9.speaker: Jesus
Luke 20:9.text: Then He proceeded to tell the people this parable: “A man planted a vineyard, rented it out to some tenants, and went away for a long time.

Luke 20:10.speaker: Jesus
Luke 20:10.text: At harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard. But the tenants beat the servant and sent him away empty-handed.

Luke 20:11.speaker: Jesus
Luke 20:11.text: So he sent another servant, but they beat him and treated him shamefully, sending him away empty-handed.

Luke 20:12.speaker: Jesus
Luke 20:12.text: Then he sent a third, but they wounded him and threw him out.

Luke 20:13.speaker: Jesus
Luke 20:13.text: ‘What shall I do?’ asked the owner of the vineyard. ‘I will send my beloved son. Perhaps they will respect him.’

Luke 20:14.speaker: Jesus
